Pierce came up lame on a route on the final play of the first quarter and was escorted to the medical tent by the training staff. He appeared to be unable to put any weight on the injured leg. It’s obviously not what fantasy managers want to see after he missed most of the offseason program following surgery on the ankle and heel on the same leg in late March. He remained in the medical tent for about 10 minutes before being carted to the locker room. Pierce caught his lone target for 11 yards prior to departing.

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that there is “optimism” that Seahawks RB Jadarian Price (chest) avoided a significant injury.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

Price reportedly underwent X-rays after the game, and the results came back negative. That’s good. The rookie running back exited during the fourth quarter in Seattle’s Week 2 game against the Cardinals and was next seen pacing the sidelines without his helmet and pads. He was later shown pointing to his right pectoral while interacting with coach Mike Macdonald. Price will undergo more testing tomorrow. Backup RBs Emanuel Wilson and Georgel Holani would split touches if Price misses the Seahawks’ Week 3 game against the Commanders.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Chris Bell didn’t catch his only target in a Week 2 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

It’s been a slow start to the season for Bell, who played on 21 of Miami’s 56 snaps and ran a route on 11 of their 30 dropbacks. That being said, many people expected Bell to start the season on the PUP list after tearing his ACL last year in college. The fact that he was healthy for Week 1 and was allegedly not on a snap count caused us to maybe get our hopes up too quickly. The 22-year-old is a talented receiver and could likely end the season as the Dolphins’ best option, but he’s going to take some time to build up to the role.

item.title: Caleb Douglas caught 2-of-3 targets for 19 yards in a Week 2 loss to the 49ers before sustaining an ankle injury.
item.description:
Caleb Douglas MIA Wide Receiver

Douglas left the stadium in a walking boot, and while it is likely precautionary, it’s certainly something to monitor. The rookie got his ankle rolled up on while blocking late in the second half. He did escape being pinned quickly and was walking on the sideline, so perhaps it’s not a serious injury. Douglas appears to have the WR1 role for the Dolphins, playing on 51 of the team’s 56 snaps and running a route on 26 of Malik Willis’ 30 dropbacks, even counting the time missed with the ankle injury. The results may not be there early on, but Douglas remains worth a bench stash given his role.

item.title: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-3 targets for 24 yards in the Commanders’ Week 2 loss to the Cowboys.
item.description:
Antonio Williams WAS Wide Receiver

Williams tied Dyami Brown for the second-most routes run (24) by any Commanders receiver, but he saw one fewer target than he did in his rookie debut. The rookie receiver came up short on an opportunity for a wide-open touchdown pass to Terry McLaurin on a trick play, which was the closest he came to generating a big play in this one. All three of Williams’ targets came on the second-to-last drive of the game for the Commanders. There’s far too much target competition here to consider Williams a viable fantasy asset in Week 3’s game against the Seahawks.

item.title: Malik Washington caught 4-of-5 targets for 43 yards in a Week 2 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Malik Washington MIA Wide Receiver

Washington led the Dolphins’ receivers in targets and was leading the team in receiving yards before one garbage time pass to Ryan Miller. Washington played on 43 of the team’s 56 snaps and ran a route on 26 of their 30 dropbacks, so he has the second-biggest role among the receivers. The issue is that he is not seeing passing down the field, and the Dolphins appear to be unable to move the ball. It’s not a situation to attack outside of the deepest fantasy formats.

item.title: De’Von Achane rushed 20 times for 74 yards in a Week 2 loss to the 49ers, adding 19 receiving yards on three catches.
item.description:
De'Von Achane MIA Running Back

Achane is the Dolphins’ entire offense, but, unfortunately, opponents know as well. He still looks explosive when he has the ball in his hands and has enough wiggle to make a few defenders miss, but there are defenders cramped in the box every time he touches the ball. The Dolphins try to get him the ball sometimes in the passing game, but he caught just three of six targets from Malik Willis, and those two are not on the same page yet. The positive news is that Achane played on 45 of the team’s 56 snaps and ran a route on 18 of the team’s 30 dropbacks, so he is going to be on the field a lot. It’s hard to envision him finding more running room next week against the Chiefs though.

item.title: Brenton Strange caught both of his targets for 17 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Brenton Strange

Strange ran a pass route on 30 of the team’s 36 drop backs but was invisible for most of the game. For now Strange can be treated as a desperation streamer in 12-team formats ahead of the Jags’ Week 3 matchup against the Patriots. He should remain on waiver wires in 10-team leagues.

item.title: Jake Ferguson caught 4-of-4 targets for 43 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 2 win over the Commanders.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

Ferguson connected with Dak Prescott for a 10-yard touchdown in the second quarter when he broke free in the secondary for an uncontested score. After a recovered fumble by the Cowboys in the third quarter,, he and Prescott would link up again for a 12-yard score to put the Cowboys up 27-13 in a game where their team never trailed. This was a far more encouraging outing for Ferguson, who posted a disappointing 2-6-0 line in Week 1 against the Giants. He’ll be on the TE2 radar in Week 3’s game against the Ravens.

item.title: Cooper Kupp caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals.
item.description:
Cooper Kupp SEA Wide Receiver

Kupp got involved on the Seahawks’ fifth and sixth drives, but was quiet outside of that. The 33-year-old wide receiver entered the game with a back injury, though he logged two full practice sessions, so it is unlikely to have meaningfully impacted him. He nabbed his second reception during the Seahawks’ two-minute drill at the end of the first half, but he was unable to get out of bounds, allowing precious seconds to tick away. Kupp is a WR5/FLEX against the Commanders.

item.title: George Kittle caught all four of his targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in a Week 2 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Kittle looked good in this one, finding space over the middle of the field and showing good burst after the catch. That’s important considering he’s still working his way back from last year’s Achilles injury. The veteran played just three fewer snaps than Mike Evans and was fourth on the team in routes run, just one behind Christian McCaffrey. His playing time will continue to increase as the year goes on, but he looks pretty close to the George Kittle we’ve gotten used to.

item.title: Deebo Samuel Sr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 31 yards in a Week 2 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
Deebo Samuel SF Wide Receiver

Deebo also had one carry for four yards. He wasn’t needed much in this game, but Deebo played on 31 of the team’s 45 snaps and ran a route on 21 of Brock Purdy’s 26 dropbacks, both of which were the most on the team among the skill core. With Demarcus Robinson suffering a high ankle sprain, we expect Deebo to be even more involved in Week 3 against the Cardinals in what should be a closer game.

item.title: Trevor Lawrence completed 17-of-29 attempts for 189 yards and one interception in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss against the Broncos, adding two rushes for six yards.
item.description:
Trevor Lawrence

The Jaguars were relatively run-heavy against Denver a week after the Broncos were shredded by Ken Walker and the Chiefs. Lawrence mostly checked down in this one, targeting Parker Washington a team-high 12 times. Brian Thomas, Jr., meanwhile, had two untimely drops, one that appeared to frustrate Lawrence. Lawrence’s interception came on a poor throw to Washington near the sideline. He’ll look to bounce back next week against a stingy New England secondary.

item.title: Rashid Shaheed caught 3-of-6 targets for 35 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals, adding one rush for four yards.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

The Seahawks tried to get Shaheed involved early on, but he largely made his presence felt on special teams, returning two kicks for 47 yards and three punts for 29 yards. Shaheed was unable to haul in his first target on the Seahawks’ second drive. He got open on a post route from the slot on the ensuing drive, and QB Drew Lock hit him for a 23-yard gain. He caught a four-yard pass in the flats immediately after that. Later, on the sixth drive, Lock fired a pass at Shaheed 34 yards downfield, but his coverage defender grazed the ball, altering the trajectory and leading to an incompletion that went off Shaheed’s fingertips. Shaheed also fumbled the second half’s opening kick return, but his teammate recovered it and advanced the ball 30 yards downfield. Shaheed remains a big-play-dependent FLEX against the Commanders next week.

item.title: Mike Evans caught all three of his targets for 54 yards in a Week 2 win over the Dolphins.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans left this game late in the second half with a hip injury, but 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said that Evans would have come back into the game if it had been closer. The veteran didn’t have many chances in this one, but he ran a route on 18 of Purdy’s 26 dropbacks, which was the second most on the team. His 27-yard catch was also a nice catch-and-run that saw him go out of bounds on the one-yard line, just before crossing the pylon. He should be good to go against the Cardinals in Week 3.

Source: 95.7 The Game

item.title: Terry McLaurin caught 2-of-9 targets for 50 yards in the Commanders’ Week 2 loss to the Cowboys.
item.description:
Terry McLaurin WAS Wide Receiver

It could have been a much bigger day for McLaurin, who had a 20-yard touchdown overturned after it was determined he did not maintain possession. In the third quarter, McLaurin broke free down the field for what would have been an easy touchdown on a trick play, but fellow receiver Antonio Williams underthrew him, ruining another scoring opportunity. McLaurin’s nine targets are a nice bump from the four he saw in Week 1 against the Eagles, and he was targeted 20-plus yards downfield four times. He continues to look like a volatile fantasy asset, with Stefon Diggs now in town. Diggs caught five passes for 47 yards and two scores in Sunday’s game. McLaurin will settle somewhere in the WR3 ranks for next week’s game against the Seahawks.

item.title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jonathon Brooks aggravated his groin injury in Week 2 against the Falcons and is considered “day to day.”
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

The good news is that this is related to Brooks’ history of knee injuries and it sounds like he has a shot at suiting up for Week 3. The bad news is that Brooks originally suffered this groin injury during training camp and is still dealing with it two weeks into the season. Brooks only had five carries and one catch before exiting Week 2’s win over Atlanta. Even if he is healthy for next week’s game, Brooks is barely on the fantasy radar right now.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: Quinshon Judkins had 12 rushes for 21 yards in the Browns’ Week 2 win against the Bucs, adding five catches for 27 yards.
item.description:
Quinshon Judkins CLE Running Back

Judkins nearly scored a couple times inside the ten yard line, but couldn’t quite punch it in. The second-year back has a solid role if/when the Browns are able to hang with their opponents and produce sufficient neutral and positive game script. On Sunday against the Bucs, Judkins accounted for 12 of the Browns’ 15 running back carries and was targeted frequently out of the backfield as Deshaun Watson posted an aDOT of 3.6. Judkins should be a top-24 option in Week 3 against a middling Panthers defense.

item.title: KC Concepcion caught all six of his targets for 28 yards in the Browns’ Week 2 win against the Bucs, adding one rush for -6 yards.
item.description:
KC Concepcion KC Concepcion caught all six of his targets for 28 yards in the Browns’ Week 2 win against the Bucs, adding one rush for -6 yards.

The good news: Todd Monken is intent on getting the football into the hands of the shifty rookie wideout. The bad news: Designed plays have been borderline disastrous for Concepcion, who was buried for a six yard loss on a first quarter carry. Denzel Boston — who caught his second touchdown of the season — was the only Browns pass catcher to see more targets for Concepcion on Sunday. Concepcion’s role in the low-wattage Cleveland offense leaves little room for weekly upside. He should be rostered in deeper formats though.
item.rw:position: Concepcion caught all six of his targets for 28 yards in the Browns’ Week 2 win against the Bucs, adding one rush for -6 yards.

item.title: Carnell Tate caught 3-of-5 targets for 27 yards in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

Tate led the Titans’ receiver corps in snaps, catches and targets, but both Elic Ayomanor and Calvin Ridley churned up more yardage. No one had a useful day in fantasy football. Tate’s usage has been excellent through his first two NFL contests, but this severely-limited offense is predictably limiting his fantasy upside. He’s a WR4 heading into next week’s Giants road trip.

item.title: Kalif Raymond caught 5-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Vikings.
item.description:
Kalif Raymond CHI Wide Receiver

For whatever reason, Raymond again lead the Bears’ receiver corps in production, though Luther Burden did out-target him on fewer snaps. Cold comfort. Although Raymond out-snapped Burden, he was on the field 16 fewer plays than Rome Odunze. Pro Football Focus’ Nathan Jahnke charted Raymond as seeing more time in “12" personnel than his sophomore teammate. We would like to say this is bound to change going forward, but coach Ben Johnson had no problem featuring veteran Olamide Zaccheaus in 2025. Raymond is struggling to create WR4 value of his own, but he is certainly hampering Burden and Odunze’s production ahead of Week 3 against the Eagles.

item.title: Bucky Irving had 15 rushes for 80 yards in the Bucs’ Week 2 loss to the Browns, adding four catches for one yard.
item.description:
Bucky Irving TB Running Back

Irving for a second straight week functioned as the unquestioned No. 1 backfield option ahead of Kenneth Gainwell, who had two rushes and three receptions on the day. Irving had a few solid runs in the first half before the Browns put the clamps on the Tampa rushing attack and forced Baker Mayfield to beat them (he did not). While somewhat surprising, Irving’s early domination of the Bucs backfield means he’ll be a high-floor weekly running back option until proven otherwise. He gets a tough matchup in Week 2 against the Vikings.

item.title: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-4 targets for 43 yards in the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Vikings.
item.description:
Rome Odunze CHI Wide Receiver

It was Odunze’s second quiet statline in as many weeks to begin the season. The difference this time, of course, was the Bears scored only three points after dropping 59 on the Panthers in Week 1. They did attempt 35 passes, 26 of which came from Caleb Williams before he injured his hamstring midway through the fourth quarter. If Williams misses Week 3 against the Eagles as is currently looking likely, it would be difficult to jam Odunze into the WR3 ranks.

item.title: T.J. Hockenson caught 3-of-4 targets for 29 yards in the Vikings’ Week 2 win over the
item.description:
T.J. Hockenson MIN Tight End

Hockenson more or less repeated his Week 1 statline, only this time on far less passing volume for the Vikings’ offense. Carson Wentz attempted just 20 throws as the Vikes went “survive and advance” mode in weather-addled Chicago. With Kyler Murray expected to return from his concussion in Week 3 in Tampa, perhaps Hockenson can post a higher-end TE2 statline.

item.title: Pat Freiermuth caught 4-of-5 targets for 32 yards in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots.
item.description:
Pat Freiermuth PIT Tight End

Freiermuth has a hold on the Steelers’ TE1 role, getting much of Aaron Rodgers’ short-yardage looks in the flat and middle of the field. The Steelers were not in the red zone all that much, so we have yet to see the 27-year-old’s utilization near the end zone. Regardless, he is consistently a top-four pass-catching option for the team, though the fantasy ceiling is low for the Pittsburgh offense. Freiermuth is a touchdown-dependent fantasy play and will be in the low-end TE2 ranks for Week 3 against the Bengals.

item.title: Jordan Addison caught 2-of-5 targets for 21 yards in the Vikings’ Week 2 win over the Bears.
item.description:
Jordan Addison MIN Wide Receiver

It’s another disappointing statline for a wideout held without a catch in Week 1, though it was yet another game where we didn’t get to see the Vikings’ “real” offense. With Kyler Murray out with a concussion, Carson Wentz was fed to the wolves at rainy Soldier Field. Murray is expected back for Week 3 in Tampa, and with him, hopefully finally a useable statline for the Vikes’ talented No. 2 receiver.

item.title: Emeka Egbuka caught 3-of-4 targets for 16 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ Week 2 loss against the Browns.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka was oh-so-close to a big game but Baker Mayfield remained wildly inaccurate in this one. Mayfield connected with Egbuka for a short score in the first half — the only positive play in the pass game for the struggling Tampa offense. While Cade Otton led the Bucs with six targets, Egbuka remains the team’s clear No. 1 target who should bounce back sooner rather than later. He should remain in all lineups next week against the Vikings.

item.title: Deshaun Watson completed 24-of-30 attempts for 238 yards and two touchdowns in the Browns’ Week 2 win against the Bucs, adding six rushes for 23 yards.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

Watson was far more accurate than he was in Week 1’s meltdown loss to the Jaguars. He was 6.5 percent over his expected completion rate and once again hit rookie WR Denzel Boston for a long touchdown. Watson navigated the pocket well and was passably accurate on short-area throws (his 3.6 aDOT is as low as it gets for a full game’s work). His Week 2 play all but guarantees he’ll hang on to the Browns’ starting QB gig for a while before Shedeur Sanders of Dillon Gabriel get another shot under center. Watson will have superflex appeal in Week 3 against a gettable Carolina defense.

item.title: Justin Jefferson caught 3-of-6 targets for 55 yards in the Vikings’ Week 2 win over the Bears.
item.description:
Justin Jefferson MIN Wide Receiver

Jefferson caught a 30-yard pass against tight coverage on just the second play of the game, but the proceedings then quickly became a contest of wills on a rainy September day in Chicago. Carson Wentz completed all of 11 passes, though Jefferson was his leading receiver, as well as most targeted. With Kyler Murray (concussion) expected to return for Week 3 against the Bucs’ shaky defense, we will hopefully get our first extended look at the Vikings’ “real” offense.

item.title: Roman Wilson caught 5-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots.
item.description:
Roman Wilson PIT Wide Receiver

Wilson tied with rookie Germie Bernard for second-most wide receiver snaps on the team, both tallying 55 snaps. He saw mostly short-yardage targets, with his longest reception tallying nine yards. Wilson’s role is as the clear WR3 in the Steelers offense; he did not see a role increase with Michael Pittman out of the game. Playing in a low-ceiling Steelers offense, Wilson is a WR5 at best for Week 3 against the Bengals.

item.title: Germie Bernard caught 4-of-8 targets for 35 yards in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots
item.description:
Germie Bernard PIT Wide Receiver

Bernard saw increased opportunity with Michael Pittman ruled out for Week 2. He caught all four of his receptions on one drive in the second quarter but ended as the second-most targeted receiver on the team. Bernard seemed to lose much of the trust he earned with a rough bobble on an Aaron Rodgers screen pass that led to an interception in the fourth quarter. The rookie second-round pick will find fantasy relevance while Pittman is out, but is no more than a fantasy WR5 for Week 3 against the Bengals.

item.title: Kyle Monangai rushed 10 times for 47 yards in the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Vikings, adding two receptions for 11 yards.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

Monangai actually lead the Bears in rushing in adverse weather conditions at Soldier Field, though D’Andre Swift led in receiving. Monangai’s most notable play might have actually come via Swift, who lost a fumble at the one-yard line. Perhaps that will have coach Ben Johnson extra committed to getting Monangai his most important short-yardage looks. With Caleb Williams looking doubtful for Week 3 against the Eagles with a hamstring injury, we could see an even bigger dose of the Bears’ backfield than usual. Monangai remains a safe, if low-upside, RB3/FLEX.

item.title: DK Metcalf caught 4-of-9 targets for 27 yards in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

Metcalf had an inefficient day, finishing fifth on the Steelers in yards despite leading the team in targets. He was unable to get open downfield; combined with Aaron Rodgers’ struggles in aiming for chunk gains, many intermediate targets fell incomplete. Metcalf dropped a critical third-down pass in the third quarter, continuing his drop issues from last week. A second straight inefficient week despite a high volume of targets makes Metcalf a rough fantasy play moving forward. Despite Michael Pittman’s absence, the fantasy points are just not consistent for Metcalf in the Steelers passing game. He will be a low-end fantasy WR3 for Week 3 against the Bengals.

item.title: Olamide Zaccheaus caught 1-of-3 targets for three yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
item.description:
Olamide Zaccheaus ATL Wide Receiver

Zaccheaus has caught exactly one pass in each of his first two games as a Falcon. With Jahan Dotson ahead of him on the depth chart and Zachariah Branch fighting for more work, Zaccheaus is not in the FLEX mix for Week 3.

item.title: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 11 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
item.description:
Jahan Dotson ATL Wide Receiver

Dotson saw four targets for the second week in a row. He went for 19 yards on one catch last week and didn’t look any different this time around. Dotson is the team’s No. 2 receiver by routes, but there aren’t enough targets to go around after Drake London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson all get theirs. Dotson is not on the fantasy radar for Week 3.

item.title: CHGO Sports’ Adam Jahns reports that Bears QB Caleb Williams walked through the locker room under his own power, “maybe” exhibiting a “slight limp.”
item.description:
Caleb Williams CHI Quarterback

Williams exited the Bears’ 3-9, Week 2 loss to the Vikings after suffering a hamstring injury that initially had him rolling on the ground, shouting in pain. Shortly after the game, multiple Chicago beat reporters took to social media to tell fans Williams was able to walk around the locker room without crutches, though at least two reporters noted that he appears to have a slight limp. Overall, this is an encouraging first update. Williams will undergo thorough testing in the coming hours and days to determine the injury’s severity and his potential return timeline. Stay tuned.

Source: Adam Jahns

item.title: Zachariah Branch caught both of his targets for 14 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
item.description:
Zachariah Branch ATL Wide Receiver

Branch’s primary duties still come on kick and punt returns, but Kevin Stefanski made it a point to get him more involved this week. He was held without a catch or even a target in Week 1. Branch isn’t on the fantasy radar yet, but dynasty managers can be pleased with his role taking a step in the right direction.

item.title: Demarcus Robinson was carted off the field in Week 2 against the Dolphins with an ankle injury.
item.description:
Demarcus Robinson SF Wide Receiver

Robinson had three catches for 34 yards early on in this one, but appeared to hurt his ankle on a 19-yard catch in the second quarter. He tumbled down at the three-yard line and was unable to get up and get into the end zone. After he was touched down, he limped off the field and was taken into the locker room on a cart. He’s been listed as questionable to return.

Source: San Francisco 49ers

item.title: Cam Ward completed 13-of-20 passes for 183 yards in the Titans’ 24-20, Week 2 loss to the Eagles, adding four rushes for seven yards and two touchdowns.
item.description:
Cam Ward TEN Quarterback

Ward’s two scores on the ground doubled his previous career total, though he is now sitting on one passing touchdown through eight quarters. He is at least not turning the ball over, and has taken “just” five sacks. He has been so far unable to heat up his connections with offseason additions Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson, but he found Elic Ayomanor for two critical gains vs. Philly. Cutting out the negative plays was an absolutely essential first step for Ward, but he has yet to supplement them with big gains or consistent chain-moving. That included botching a Hail Mary in the fourth quarter this afternoon. Ward won’t be much of a superflex option for next week’s road date with the Giants.

item.title: Kenyon Sadiq caught 2-of-3 passes for 17 yards in the Jets’ Week 2 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Kenyon Sadiq NYJ Tight End

Not only did Sadiq not make a huge impact on the field, but he also played fewer snaps and ran fewer routes than Mason Taylor. Sadiq is an incredibly athletic and talented rookie, but he’s also 21 years old and is going to need a while to adjust to the NFL game. His role will likely increase for the Jets as the year goes on, but he figures to be inconsistent in the early part of the season.

item.title: Tyson Bagent completed 5-of-9 passes for 54 yards in the Bears’ 9-3, Week 2 loss to the Vikings.
item.description:
Tyson Bagent CHI Quarterback

Bagent checked in with 7:15 remaining after Caleb Williams suffered a non-contact injury dashing for the end zone. Bagent did his best to rally the troops in windy, rainy weather, but his lack of arm strength relative to Williams was immediately apparent. Where it at first appeared Williams was dealing with a season-ending knee or achilles’ tendon injury, he has since been diagnosed with a hamstring issue. That means that even though Williams is probably on the wrong side of questionable for Week 3 against the Eagles, Bagent may only end up making a start or two. He will be a last-gasp superflex option if forced into duty next Monday.

item.title: Jaylen Warren rushed 11 times for 43 yards in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots, adding two receptions for 34 yards.
item.description:
Jaylen Warren PIT Running Back

Warren was the second back to enter the game behind Rico Dowdle, but he operated as the lead back for much of the day with Dowdle dealing with a toe injury. He averaged just under four yards per carry as his biggest play came on a 26-yard reception. With Aaron Rodgers’ inability to consistently push the ball downfield, Warren is the primary checkdown guy to benefit, seeing four targets in Week 2 after totaling six targets in Week 1. He dominated snaps when Dowdle was out and will rank as a fantasy RB2 should Dowdle miss time. Otherwise, Warren is an RB3 for Week 3 against the Bengals.

item.title: Isaiah Williams caught all six of his targets for 34 yards in the Jets’ Week 2 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Isaiah Williams NYJ Wide Receiver

Williams operated as the clear third wide receiver, playing on 61 of the team’s 74 snaps and running a route on 43 of their 50 dropbacks, which was actually more than Adonai Mitchell. Almost all of Williams’ work is on screen passes and quick slants where he can use his speed, but if he’s going to be on the field this much, he could be a sneaky deep league play against the Lions in Week 3.

item.title: Garrett Wilson caught 5-of-7 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 2 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Garrett Wilson NYJ Wide Receiver

Wilson saw five fewer targets than Adonai Mitchell, but played more snaps and ran more routes. Mitchell simply sees more quick-hitter looks close to the line of scrimmage, while Wilson is used more over the middle of the field. The Packers also frequently sent safety help over to Wilson’s side, but the 26-year-old was still able to make a few big catches when they mattered. He should be in for a bigger day against the Lions next week.

item.title: Brian Robinson rushed 11 times for 51 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers, adding two catches for 16 yards.
item.description:
Brian Robinson ATL Running Back

Six of his 13 touches came on the final two drives of the game, after the Falcons pulled their starters. Robinson was not awfully involved in the offense before that. He is the clear backup to Bijan Robinson but nothing more.

item.title: Adonai Mitchell caught 6-of-12 passes for 63 yards in the Jets’ Week 2 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Adonai Mitchell NYJ Wide Receiver

Mitchell led the Jets in targets while playing 61 of the team’s 74 snaps and running a route on 41 of their 50 dropbacks. Mitchell was also targeted on a deep ball that led to a defensive pass interference call and would have had another 40+ yard completion if it weren’t for a truly impressive play by the Green Bay defensive back. The Jets are getting no push from their offensive line, so the team will likely need to take to the air to use the ball. That figures to be good news for Mitchell, especially next week against a banged-up Lions secondary.

item.title: Carson Wentz completed 11-of-20 passes for 143 scoreless yards in the Vikings’ 9-3, Week 2 victory over the Bears.
item.description:
Carson Wentz MIN Quarterback

Surprisingly for Wentz, he rushed only three times for six yards. Unsurprisingly, he took three sacks and a few other big hits. It was no matter, as Wentz more than did his job as he avoided turnovers so the Vikings could grind out a rainy victory in the Windy City. With Kyler Murray (concussion) expected back for Week 3 in Tampa Bay, Wentz can be returned to the waiver wire in superflex leagues.

item.title: Eli Raridon caught his lone target for 30 yards in the Patriots’ Week 2 win over the Steelers.
item.description:
Eli Raridon NE Tight End

Raridon saw 11 snaps before exiting due to a thigh injury in the first half. He caught his lone target for 30 yards, fighting through pass interference for the grab. Raridon did not re-enter the game after leaving; fantasy managers should stay tuned to the injury report next week to see how major the issue is. If healthy, Raridon is worth rostering only in the deepest of leagues for redraft formats.

item.title: Jack Strand completed 8-of-15 passes for 59 yards and an interception in the Falcons’ 34-3, Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
item.description:
Jack Strand ATL Quarterback

Strand replaced a struggling Cooper Rush in the third quarter of the blowout loss. His first career attempt was a pick-six, but it’s hard to pin much of the blame on him. He made a tight-window throw to Jahan Dotson and Devin Lloyd simply ripped the ball out of the receiver’s hands before he could secure it. Strand wasn’t awfully productive even after throwing out that play, taking two sacks while averaging a pitiful 3.9 yards per attempt. The hope for Falcons fans and fantasy managers alike is that Michael Penix will be ready for Week 3. It’s unclear whether Strand or Rush would start if Penix and Tua Tagovailoa remain out.

item.title: Breece Hall rushed 16 times for 29 yards in the Jets’ Week 2 loss to the Packers, adding 63 yards receiving on five catches.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

Hall couldn’t get anything going on the ground, and that was mainly on the offensive line, which got no push against the Packers’ defensive front. More troubling was that Hall played on 48 of the team’s 74 snaps and ceded work to Braelon Allen, including a goal-line touchdown run. Hall’s receiving ability will help him save some fantasy value, and his 43-yard reception was basically all thanks to his ability after the catch, but the offensive line and Allen may keep Hall as a low-end RB2 unless his role changes.

item.title: Packers WR Jayden Reed (neck) has feeling and movement in all of his extremities.
item.description:
Jayden Reed GB Wide Receiver

This is an encouraging first update on the Packers’ injured wide receiver. Reed will stay overnight at the hospital for further testing and observation, according to the team. Reed suffered a neck injury early in the Packers’ Week 2 game against the Jets and was taken to the locker room on a stretcher. Hopefully, the positive reports continue rolling in.

Source: Green Bay Packers

item.title: Tucker Kraft caught 2-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets.
item.description:
Tucker Kraft GB Tight End

The good news is that Kraft played 52 of the team’s 53 snaps and ran a route on 32 of their 34 dropbacks. The bad news is that he wasn’t commanding targets, and he also fumbled one of his catches, but the replay review couldn’t determine for sure who recovered it, so the Packers were able to maintain possession. Perhaps we should have been a little less aggressive in expecting Kraft to return from tearing his ACL less than a year ago and go right back to being himself at the start of the season. His role remains elite, but it may take another couple of weeks before he’s physically able to play like we’re used to seeing.

item.title: Hunter Henry caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Patriots’ Week 2 win over the Steelers.
item.description:
Hunter Henry NE Tight End

Henry was the Patriots’ primary tight end, leading all pass-catchers in targets on the day. He totaled 40 yards on three catches as part of a receiving-by-committee approach by the Drake Maye passing attack. His role is isolated despite Eli Raridon slowly taking on some more routes to open the season. Henry is a fantasy TE2 for Week 3 against the Jaguars.

item.title: Jared Wayne caught 2-of-7 targets for 33 yards in Houston’s Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
item.description:
Jared Wayne HOU Wide Receiver

Jaylin Noel outsnapped him 44-to-36 for the Texans No. 3 receiver role but Wayne beat Noel out by one catch, two yards, and two targets. “Man starts over again everyday, in spite of all he knows, against all he knows,” Emil Cioran once wrote. And these are the readings C.J. Stroud should get familiar with as he endures another week of this receiving corps in Week 3.

item.title: Aaron Jones rushed 23 times for 105 yards in the Vikings’ Week 2 win over the Bears.
item.description:
Aaron Jones MIN Running Back

Jones was not targeted in the passing game. Jones was also announced with a knee injury in the second half, but played through the issue to earn his first 100-yard rushing effort since 2024. It was a much, much needed outing with Jordan Mason on injured reserve and the Vikings trying to grind out a rainy victory in Chicago. It’s possible Jones could need further testing this week, but the fact that he finished the game obviously suggests he will be on the right side of questionable for Week 3 against the Bucs. With neither DeeJay Dallas nor Demond Claiborne making an impact vs. the Bears, Jones will be a safe RB2 if he can get out there next Sunday.

item.title: Matthew Golden caught 4-of-6 targets for 58 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets.
item.description:
Matthew Golden GB Wide Receiver

Golden ran a route on 32 of the team’s 34 dropbacks and was the target on a few deep passes that led to pass interference penalties. This was not an efficient passing day for the Packers’ offense, but it was nice to see Golden be such a huge part of it. With Jayden Reed (neck) getting hurt in this game and Tucker Kraft still not seemingly playing at 100 percent, Golden is the clear second target in this offense. He could be in for a big game against the Falcons in Week 3.

item.title: Xavier Legette caught 2-of-4 targets for 64 yards in the Panthers’ Week 2 win over the Falcons.
item.description:
Xavier Legette CAR Wide Receiver

Legette beat Atlanta deep for a 55-yard gain at the end of the second quarter. The catch set up an eventual Darren Waller touchdown. While Legette isn’t on the fantasy radar heading into Week 3, he seems to have carved out a solid role as the Panthers’ No. 3 receiver.

item.title: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-9 targets for 37 yards in Houston’s Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
item.description:
Xavier Hutchinson HOU Wide Receiver

Through two games, Hutchinson has 15 targets and 69 yards. If you’re going to be this bad, you at least want the meme number. Hutchinson let a (admittedly hard to reel in) C.J. Stroud ball hit him in the hands in the end zone before dropping it and repeatedly struggled to reel in balls, as he did in Week 1. Hutchinson is a fine depth receiver who has been pushed into a role he simply can’t do at the NFL level.

item.title: Darren Waller caught all three of his targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 2 win over the Falcons.
item.description:
Darren Waller CAR Tight End

Waller saw as many targets as Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans combined. Unlike the other Carolina tight ends, Waller is still an explosive pass-catcher and a de facto wide receiver. When Bryce Young looked his way, it was for a big play. He made good on the minor role with his first two touchdowns as a Panther. Waller only has five targets through two weeks. He will make the occasional big play, but it’s hard to get him in fantasy lineups with such a limited role.

item.title: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-4 targets for 66 yards in the Saints’ Week 2 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Juwan Johnson NO Tight End

Johnson was on the receiving end of two big plays in Sunday’s win over the Ravens. Johnson hauled in a short pass on a third-and-13 in the third quarter and turned it upfield for a 25-yard gain. In the fourth quarter, Johnson again picked up 25 yards on a short pass on third-and-eight, taking it to the Ravens’ five-yard line and setting the Saints up for a touchdown a few plays later. Johnson has caught seven passes in his first two games and is averaging an impressive 17.1 YPR on said catches. He’ll be on the TE2 radar for next week’s game against the Raiders.

item.title: Devaughn Vele caught 5-of-7 targets for 64 yards in the Saints’ Week 2 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Devaughn Vele NO Wide Receiver

It was another solid outing for Vele, who has now caught 12 passes for 133 yards and one touchdown in his first two games this season. Vele’s biggest play came on a third-and-eight when he hauled in a 29-yard reception to extend a drive that ended with a Daniel Carlson field goal. Vele is the clear-cut WR2 for the Saints at this point and could be worth a dart throw in deeper leagues next week as a WR3/WR4 in Week 3 against the Raiders.

item.title: Mark Andrews caught 6-of-7 yargets for 49 yards in the Ravens’ Week 2 loss to the Saints.
item.description:
Mark Andrews BAL Tight End

Andrews was targeted four times on the Ravens’ first four possessions, with his biggest play coming on a 10-yard reception to start a drive that ended with a Derrick Henry touchdown. Andrews caught a 14-yard reception on the Ravens’ final drive of the game as they tried to mount a comeback, but the drive ended on an interception by Lamar Jackson three plays later. Andrews has caught 10 passes for 98 scoreless yards on 13 targets through his first two games. It’s decent production for a tight end, but he continues to look like a shell of the player he once was. He’ll be a boom-or-bust TE2 in Week 3 against the Cowboys.

item.title: DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Patriots’ Week 2 win over the Steelers.
item.description:
DeMario Douglas NE Wide Receiver

Douglas made the first catch of the game for the Patriots, but was silent the rest of the day. The 25-year-old is a low-yardage slot receiver who tends to get schemed targets when he is on the field. Douglas tallied the third-most snaps of all Patriots wide receivers on the day but will find it hard to achieve fantasy relevancy in an offense that utilizes multiple receivers in several different ways. Second-year receiver Kyle Williams also saw a pair of targets, catching one for 10 yards. Neither Williams or Douglas are anything more than deep league dart throws for Week 3 against the Jaguars.

item.title: Kaleb Johnson rushed eight times for 32 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets.
item.description:
Kaleb Johnson GB Running Back

Johnson actually led the Packers in rushing attempts and rushing yards in this one. He played on just 13 of the team’s 53 snaps, so we’re not going to get ahead of ourselves here, but he was also clearly the team’s best running back on the day, and he took the first carries in overtime after Marshawn Lloyd fumbled in the second half. There’s a real chance that Johnson steps into a bigger role in Week 3 against Atlanta. He deserves to be added in deeper formats just in case that comes to fruition.

item.title: Chuba Hubbard rushed 12 times for 53 yards in the Panthers’ Week 2 win over the Falcons, adding two catches for 11 yards and a touchdown.
item.description:
Chuba Hubbard CAR Running Back

Hubbard operated as the Panthers’ unquestioned RB1, out-carrying Jonathon Brooks 12-5. He got on the board early with a touchdown catch near the goal line. It was his second touchdown grab of the year and his third time finding the end zone in total. Brook also left the game early with a groin injury and his status for Week 3 is up in the air. Hubbard was already going to project for RB2 numbers with Brooks in the middle. He will push to the middle of the RB2 pack if Brooks is out versus the Browns.

item.title: Dalton Schultz caught 12-of-14 targets for 140 yards in Houston’s Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
item.description:
Dalton Schultz HOU Tight End

An incredible PPR scam as the Texans had him as the main checkdown receiver while trailing for much of the game. Eight of the 12 catches came in the fourth quarter as C.J. Stroud tried in vain to push the rest of this offense anywhere. Don’t expect this much next week with Collins apparently questionable again, but Schultz clearly elevates in the pecking order and has TE1 appeal.

item.title: Luther Burden caught 3-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Vikings.
item.description:
Luther Burden CHI Wide Receiver

For the second straight week, Burden was out-produced by Kalif Raymond, who again led the receiver corps in production. D’Andre Swift “led” the entire team in receiving with five receptions for 54 scoreless yards. Burden is now sitting on eight catches for 95 yards through two weeks. It’s not the worst start anyone has ever seen, but fantasy managers were expecting better. It might not be coming in Week 3 if Caleb Williams’ hamstring injury costs him time against the Eagles, which seems highly likely. We are trying not to overreact to small-sample sizes, but Burden is definitely now more of a WR3 than WR2 heading into next Monday’s contest. That, of course, should still have him in most fantasy lineups.

item.title: Chris Brooks rushed four times for 11 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets.
item.description:
Chris Brooks GB Running Back

He added one catch for 15 yards. While those stats are not impressive, Brooks also played on 24 of the team’s 53 snaps, which was the most of any Green Bay running back. After Marshawn Lloyd fumbled in the second half, it was Brooks who saw the next red zone carries and also Brooks who caught a crucial pass in overtime to set up the game-winning field goal. This has all the makings of a confusing committee, but Brooks needs to be on radars in deeper formats until Josh Jacobs returns.

item.title: Mack Hollins caught 2-of-2 targets for 18 yards in the Patriots’ Week 2 win over the Steelers.
item.description:
Mack Hollins NE Wide Receiver

Hollins quietly led Patriots wide receivers in snaps in the first game without A.J. Brown. He saw just two targets on the day, catching both for a total of 18 yards in a subpar offensive day. The Pats pass-catchers are a mix of low-ceiling fantasy viability as Maye spreads the wealth around the different receivers. Better offensive days are ahead for the Patriots but Hollins is a WR5 play at best for Week 3 against the Jaguars.

item.title: Marshawn Lloyd rushed six times for 20 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets, adding six yards receiving and a touchdown.
item.description:
MarShawn Lloyd GB Running Back

Perhaps more importantly, Lloyd lost a key fumble in the second half and then was barely on the field after that. The 25-year-old had plenty of trouble earning yards in the running game, but he was wide open on a well-designed screen pass in the first half for a touchdown catch. Lloyd played on just 16 of the Packers’ 53 snaps and handled seven of their 19 carries. This is a confusing committee that isn’t giving any running back real value, and Josh Jacobs could return at some point near the middle of the season. Fantasy managers in shallow leagues don’t need to hold onto Lloyd, and others could look to trade him away on the back of his receiving touchdown.

item.title: Steelers RB Rico Dowdle (toe) returned to Week 2 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Rico Dowdle PIT Running Back

Dowdle took a cart from the medical tent to the locker room in the second quarter but returned to the game after halftime. Travis Homer saw a couple carries while Dowdle was out, but the backfield returns to a Dowdle/Jaylen Warren split now.

item.title: Brock Bowers (knee) will not play in Week 2 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Bowers returned to practice on Friday but was listed as doubtful. He is eyeing a Week 3 return. Michael Mayer will draw the start again this week. Also inactive for the Raiders are CB Darien Porter, QB Aidan O’Connell, S Tristin McCollum, S Dalton Johnson, G Bryce Cabeldue, and DT JJ Pegues,

item.title: Ladd McConkey (rib) is active for Week 2 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

McConkey was trending toward playing as of this morning and made it through pregame workouts without any issues. He will wear a protective jacket for this game and will likely play fewer than his normal number of snaps. Fantasy managers can move him down the WR2 ranks because of the injury, but it’s hard to pull him out of lineups entirely. Inactive for the Chargers are S Elijah Molden, CB Deane Leonard, CB Isas Waxter, OL Logan Taylor, OL Alex Harkey, and OL Trey Pipkins III.

item.title: Saquon Barkley (stinger) returned for the second half of the Eagles’ Week 2 game against the Titans.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley seemed like he was dying to get back into the game in the second quarter, but he couldn’t get comfortable. That evidently changed at halftime. We will undoubtedly see more Tank Bigsby than usual in quarters three and four, but Barkley’s return is the best possible news after he was roughed up on the Eagles’ opening drive.

item.title: Steelers RB Rico Dowdle (toe) was carted to the locker room in Week 2 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Rico Dowdle PIT Running Back

Dowdle was hurt on an Aaron Rodgers fumble that lost 37 yards in the second quarter. He hobbled to the medical tent and was later carted to the locker room from there. Dowdle is questionable to return with a toe injury in Week 3 against the Patriots.

item.title: Patriots OL Michael Onwenu was carted off in Week 2 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Michael Onwenu NE Guard

Onwenu was rolled up on by a Steelers defender in the second quarter of the Patriots’ Week 2 game against the Steelers. His right leg was caught in a gruesome way and the cart came out for the 28-year-old; he was promptly ruled out of the game with an ankle injury. Greg Van Roten comes in for Onwenu at right guard.

item.title: Dallas Goedert suffered a right knee injury in the Eagles’ Week 2 game against the Titans and is questionable to return.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

Goedert got roughed up run blocking early in the second quarter. He was then absent for the following drive, earning the questionable tag. It’s not a good development for someone with Goedert’s injury history, though to the naked eye, it did not have the looks of a season-ending injury. Goedert had a four-yard catch on two targets before departing. Johnny Mundt is the next man up at tight end. Second-round rookie Eli Stowers (quad, hamstring) is currently on injured reserve.

Source: Jimmy Kempski

item.title: Saquon Barkley (stinger) is questionable to return to the Eagles’ Week 2 game against the Titans.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley was injured on the Eagles’ opening drive and immediately announced as questionable. He returned to the Eagles’ sideline in relatively short order with his helmet and a neck roll, but he has remained sidelined into the second quarter. He has also since shed his helmet. It appears it could be Tank Bigsby closing this one out for the Eagles. The only good news is, a stinger would be unlikely to sideline Barkley for Week 3. Stay tuned.

item.title: Zach Bako-Bewele (leg) was carted off the field in Week 2 against the Jets.
item.description:
Zach Bako-Bewele GB Offensive Lineman

Just one play after Jayden Reed (neck) was placed on a stretcher, the Packers also lost their starting right tackle. Bako-Bewele was blocking on a third-down play, when it appeared his feet got either tackled up with Jordan Love or stuck in the turf at MetLife. He was down in immense pain and had to have his leg in an air cast when he was taken off the field. It had the look of a serious injury, and he was immediately ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Source: Matt Schneidman

item.title: Jayden Reed was taken off the field on a stretcher in Week 2 against the Jets.
item.description:
Jayden Reed GB Wide Receiver

On just the second play of the game, Reed was tackled on a screen pass and was twisted around. There didn’t appear to be any direct contact to his head, but he went limp when he hit the ground in a scary scene. He was placed on a spine board, taken off the field on a cart, and immediately ruled out for the remainder of the game. After the game, we should learn more about the nature of his injury.

Source: Matt Schneidman

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said Shedeur Sanders could start in Week 3 if Deshaun Watson plays poorly in Week 2.
item.description:
Shedeur Sanders CLE Quarterback

Schefter said it “feels like Shedeur’s time is coming” if Watson bombs in the Browns’ Week 2 matchup with the Bucs following his Week 1 collapse against Jacksonville. Sanders, in that scenario, would be under center for the Browns’ home opener against the Panthers in Week 3. Sanders, who is slightly more accurate than Watson in the short and intermediate areas, would be an upgrade for Harold Fannin and KC Concepcion. He would likely be a downgrade for downfield air yards eater Denzel Boston.

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Lions have checked in on CB Kenny Moore.
item.description:
Kenny Moore

Moore was released in May after requesting a trade and has been a free agent ever since, without even a visit to his name. Garafolo reports multiple teams have inquired on Moore and he’s expected to sign in the near future.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Steelers are planning for Joey Porter (back) to return in Week 3 but whether or not he does return “is a bit more ambiguous.”
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

This situation looks like it remains touch-and-go as the “business angle to this situation that cannot be ignored as the sides remain at an impasse in contract discussions” continues. Obviously, it would be enormous for the Steelers if they had a healthy Porter for JaMarr Chase and Tee Higgins in Week 3. Whether that happens remains to be seen.

item.title: Trey Hendrickson (finger) will play in Week 2 against the Saints.
item.description:
Trey Hendrickson BAL Outside Linebacker

Hendrickson reportedly broke his finger “into several pieces,” but that won’t be enough to keep him out against his former team this week. Ravens writer Ryan Mink said Hendrickson’s fingers are “heavily wrapped” and that he’ll play with a cast on.

Source: Ryan Mink

item.title: Packers declared CB Benjamin St-Juste, OL John Williams, OL Travis Glover, DT Warren Brinson, and DT Javon Hargrave inactive for Week 2 against the Jets.
item.description:
Aaron Banks GB Guard

That means that starting left guard Aaron Banks (knee) will be back on the field after missing Week 1 against the Vikings. In a game that figures to be played in constant rain, having a fully healthy offensive line will be a nice boost for Marshawn Lloyd and the Packers’ offense. Javon Hargrave (concussion) remains out for Week 2.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Puka Nacua (groin) is “trending in the wrong direction” for Week 2.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Schefter said on Sunday NFL Countdown that Nacua is more likely to be sidelined on Monday against the Giants than he is to suit up and play through his groin injury. It would be a massive blow to the Rams offense, which would likely be more run-heavy if Nacua is out against the Giants. That could mean a big workload for Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Terrance Ferguson, who ran a route on just 41 percent of the Rams’ drop backs in Week 1, could see a slightly bigger role if Nacua is sidelined.

item.title: Jets declared CB D’Angelo Ponds, S Minkah Fitzpatrick, RB Kene Nwangwu, ED Joseph Ossai, LB Trevin Wallace, and K Blake Grupe inactive for Week 2 against the Packers.
item.description:
D'Angelo Ponds NYJ Cornerback

We knew Fitzpatrick had already been ruled out with a groin injury. D’Angelo Pounds had practiced all week, and Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that he was healthy enough to play, but apparently there is no room for him in the secondary at the moment. The good news for the Jets is that Will McDonald (ankle) is active and will play.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. (back) is inactive for Week 2 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

Porter was declared out on Friday due to a back issue that also kept him out of Week 1. With his contract situation also up in the air, it is unclear if Porter will return in Week 3. Also inactive for the Steelers are WR Michael Pittman Jr., QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, OG Gennings Dunker, DL Kevin Jobity Jr., and DE Gabriel Rubio. Pittman was ruled out with a foot injury while Howard will serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback.

item.title: Texans declared WR Nico Collins inactive for Houston’s Week 2 game against the Bengals.
item.description:
Nico Collins HOU Wide Receiver

He had already been ruled out and is in jeopardy of missing Week 3 as well. The Texans ruled out Collins, Jadeveon Clowney (knee), Jake Hummel (groin) and Ed Ingram (groin) on Friday. Joining them as healthy scratches are TE Brevin Jordan, CB Collin Wright, and T Nate Thomas.

item.title: Sean Tucker (hamstring) is active for Week 2 against the Browns.
item.description:
Sean Tucker TB Running Back

Tucker was out last week with the hamstring issue. His return to the Tampa lineup could take a few touches away from Bucky Irving and/or Kenneth Gainwell. Last week against the Bengals, Irving out-carried Gainwell 8-5 and led the backfield with a 59 percent route share. Bucs declared CB Jacob Parrish, CB Ayden Garnes, DL Elijah Simmons, DL DeMonta Capehart, OL Billy Schrauth, and OL Luke Haggard inactive for Week 2.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Eagles declared QB Tanner McKee, QB Cole Payton, WR Elijah Moore, EDGE Jonathan Greenard (pectoral), and OT Micah Morris inactive for Philadelphia’s Week 2 game against the Titans.
item.description:
Tanner McKee PHI Quarterback

Greenard was ruled out on Friday after three limited practices; there’s a chance he returns next week. Andrew Mukuba (knee) is playing off a questionable tag. Everyone else here is a healthy scratch.

item.title: Kendre Miller is inactive for Week 2 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Kendre Miller NO Running Back

Miller will be a healthy scratch with Alvin Kamara officially back for Week 2. Miller rushed nine times for 30 yards and a touchdown in Week 1 against the Lions, but he looks like the odd man out with the Saints’ top two backs healthy; rookie CJ Donaldson, who contributes on special teams, will serve as the team’s RB3. Miller’s fantasy value is non-existent as long as Kamara and Travis Etienne are both dressing on Sundays.

Source: New Orleans Saints

item.title: Patriots CB Carlton Davis (neck) is inactive for Week 2 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Carlton Davis NE Cornerback

Davis did not practice all week due to a neck injury and was officially ruled out on Saturday. The Patriots will look for reinforcements in the secondary for Week 2 against the Steelers. Also inactive for the Patriots are OT Dametrious Crownover, OT Walter Rouse, TE Tanner Arkin, DT Leonard Taylor, and QB Behren Morton.

item.title: Panthers declared OLB Pat Jones, TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, CB Chau Smith-Wade, LB Tyrel Dodson, OT Albert Reese, and DT Bobby Brown inactive for Week 2 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Patrick Jones CAR Outside Linebacker

Jones missed most of the 2025 season with a back injury and subsequent surgery. He was also held out of Week 1. Jones was back at practice this week, but the team is going to give him a few more practices before letting him take the field again.

item.title: Chris Olave (hamstring) is active for Week 2 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Chris Olave NO Wide Receiver

Olave is officially active after popping up on Thursday’s injury report with a hamstring issue. He logged a limited practice Friday, so hopefully he won’t be too hampered in what could be a high-scoring game. Assuming a normal workload, Olave projects as a solid WR1. While Olave is active, the Saints did declare RB Kendre Miller, QB Zach Wilson, CB Decamerion Richardson, LB Isaiah Stalbird, DL Christen Miller, OL Mason Murphy, and DL John Ridgeway III inactive for Week 2.

Source: New Orleans Saints

item.title: Titans declared CB Cor’Dale Flott (quad) inactive for Tennessee’s Week 2 game against the Eagles.
item.description:
Cor'Dale Flott TEN Cornerback

He popped up on the injury report on Friday with a quad injury and was listed as questionable. Also inactive for the Titans are: LB james Williams (elbow), G Atonio Mafi, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE Kylen Granson, and DT Jackie Marshall.

item.title: Bears OT Ozzy Trapilo is inactive for Week 2 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Ozzy Trapilo CHI Offensive Lineman

Trapilo was actually removed from the final injury report, but The Athletic reports he is still not game ready after rupturing his patellar tendon last season. It is unclear when that might be, but Trapilo is at least now trending toward contributing at some point this season. Also inactive for the Bears are QB Case Keenum, DL Jayden Loving, DL Jamree Kromah and OL Jordan McFadden.

item.title: Browns C Elgton Jenkins (back) is active for Week 2 against the Bucs.
item.description:
Elgton Jenkins CLE Offensive Lineman

Jenkins missed some practice time this week with a lingering back issue. He’ll suit up against a Tampa defense that last week pressured the passer at a lowly 24 percent rate. Browns declared QB Taylen Green, LB Justin Jefferson, S Daniel Thomas, CB Toriano Pride Jr., C Parker Brailsford, and G Teven Jenkins inactive for Week 2.

item.title: Ravens declared WR Zay Flowers, LB Teddye Buchanan, OG Andrew Voorhees, OT Gerad Lichtenhan, DT Nnamdi Madubuike, and QB Joe Fagnano inactive for Week 2 against the Saints.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Flowers was officially ruled out on Saturday by the team, so there’s nothing too surprising to see here. Veteran receiver Rashod Bateman is expected to see an increased role with Flowers sidelined, while Devontez Walker is also active after being a healthy scratch in Week 1 against the Colts. If possible, it would be best to avoid all Ravens receivers in fantasy this week.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: A.J. Terrell (shoulder) is active for Week 2 against the Panthers.
item.description:
A.J. Terrell ATL Cornerback

Chris Lindstrom cleared concussion protocol over the weekend and is also active. Inactive for the Falcons are QB Tua Tagovailoa, QB Michael Penix Jr., DB Billy Bowman Jr., DB Malcolm DeWalt IV, and OL Ethan Onianwa.

item.title: Vikings declared QB Kyler Murray, WR, Jauan Jennings, CB Zemaiah Vaughn, S Jakobe Thomas, C Nick Samac, OT Caleb Tiernan and DL Elijah Williams inactive for Week 2 against the Bears.
item.description:
Kyler Murray MIN Quarterback

ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported Sunday morning Murray is “on track” to return in Week 3 against the Bucs. Jennings, who is out for non-football reasons, has a less clear return timeline.

item.title: Joe Burrow (back) is active for Cincinnati’s Week 2 game against the Texans.
item.description:
Joe Burrow CIN Quarterback

It never seemed like there was a real chance Burrow would miss this game, even after Josh Johnson was elevated from the practice squad yesterday. Burrow will be on the QB1 line against a Texans defense looking to rebound. Inactive for the Bengals are: Johnson, WR Ke’Shawn Williams, CB Josh Newton, C Connor Lew, OL Myles Hinton, DT B.J. Hill (Achilles), and DT Landon Robinson.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Kyler Murray (concussion) “is on track” to play in Week 3 against the Bucs.
item.description:
Kyler Murray MIN Quarterback

Schefter added that Murray is expected to clear concussion protocol next week. He was limited throughout practice this week before being ruled out on Friday. Murray made progress through the protocol during the week but couldn’t get the green light before the weekend. Carson Wentz will make one more start. Even with another strong showing, Wentz is all but certain to return to backup duties once Murray is healthy.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ed Oliver (hip) “has a chance” to play in Week 3 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Ed Oliver BUF Defensive Lineman

He is considered day-to-day. Per Rapoport, Oliver experienced hip spasms during warmups ahead of the Bills’ Week 2 game against the Lions. The Bills ruled him out right at the deadline for inactives. Oliver only appeared in three games last year but still managed three sacks. He logged one TFL and a fumble recovery in Week 1 of this year.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports DJ Moore (shoulder) is considered “day-to-day” and is expected to practice next week.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

Moore is believed to have suffered an AC joint sprain in Week 2. He left in the first half after landing on his shoulder and did not return. His status for Week 3 remains up in the air, but an immediate return to practice would be a good sign. He got off to a hot start in Week 1 with 100 yards and a touchdown before being shut out in his brief Week 2 showing. The extra rest between Thursday’s game and Buffalo’s upcoming matchup with the Chargers will hopefully be enough to get more back on the field.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Week 4 is the “more likely” target for Sam Darnold (glute) to return.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

Rapoport did note that Darnold is expected to practice in some capacity next week. It sounds like the team will use next week’s sessions to give him an extended ramp-up ahead of Week 4, though a Week 3 return isn’t out of the question. Drew Lock will start this week and probably next week as well. He is in the QB2 mix for Superflex leagues, though managers without a second quarterback spot don’t need to worry about Lock for now.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports “the belief is that the first two games would serve as a natural evaluation point” for Deshaun Watson.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

The Browns open the year with a two-game road trip before returning to Cleveland for their home opener next week. Watson was a disaster in Week 1, turning the ball over twice while throwing for 205 yards and one score. Another showing like that versus the Bucs this week and he could be sent to the bench. Shedeur Sanders would then draw the start against Carolina in Week 3. It’s unlikely the Browns offense turns things around under Sanders, but things truly cannot get worse than they are right now.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Michael Penix (knee) could play in Week 3 against the Packers.
item.description:
Michael Penix ATL Quarterback

Per Schefter and Ian Rapoport, Penix is the team’s preferred starter and is nearing a return. Once he is finally ready to suit up, the job is his. They also note that the Falcons won’t cut Tua Tagovailoa, even once the team has four healthy quarterbacks. There is a possibility that a team wants to trade for Tua ahead of the midseason deadline, though we’re skeptical that there’s much of a market for him after this disastrous start to the season.

Source: ESPN

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Trey Hendrickson (finger) is “slated to play” in Week 2 against the Saints.
item.description:
Trey Hendrickson BAL Outside Linebacker

Rapoport notes that Hendruckson broke his finger “into several pieces this week.” Ouch. He will play with a cast on his hand for Week 2 and likely much longer. With Hendrickson available, the Ravens’ defense is one of the better fantasy options versus a pass-happy Saints offense this week.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chris Jones (calf) “should be good to go” for Week 2 against the Colts.
item.description:
Chris Jones KC Defensive Tackle

Jones was limited in practice throughout the week, though it was likely little more than maintenance for the NFL veteran. The Chiefs are also expected to have first-round rookie Mansoor Delane available for Sunday Night Football.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chase Young (calf) is expected to play in Week 2 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Chase Young NO Defensive End

Young experienced some soreness in his calf during the week and left Thursday’s practice early. His departure was considered precautionary, though the team ultimately listed him as questionable for Week 2 on Friday. Having Young available is a good start for a Saints defense trying to slow down Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chris Lindstrom (concussion) is expected to play in Week 2 against the
item.description:
Chris Lindstrom ATL Guard

Atlanta is also going to have AJ Terrell (shoulder) available for Week 2. Both players were listed as questionable on Friday. It’s a good start for Atlanta, but what the team really needs is a healthy quarterback. Even third-stringer Cooper Rush is playing through a back injury, and the results were downright pitiful in Week 1.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Joe Burrow (back) will play in Week 2 against the Texans.
item.description:
Joe Burrow CIN Quarterback

The Bengals called up Josh Johnson from the practice squad over the weekend, raising some eyebrows regarding Burrow’s health. The move, however, was purely a precaution. Burrow has already said he is playing this week. He remains near the top of the QB1 ranks despite a tough matchup with the Houston defense.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Broncos maintain a “high level of confidence and comfort” in offensive coordinator Davis Webb.
item.description:
Davis Webb DEN Coaching Staff

Webb took over play-calling duties from Sean Payton this year. The results were disastrous in Week 1. Denver scored 10 points against the Chiefs, Bo Nix was held to 131 yards, and Jaylen Waddle caught one pass all night. It’s a little early for the Broncos to be reminding us that switching to Webb as play-caller wasn’t a bad decision, but the Week 1 results were alarming. If the team continues to struggle on offense, Payton could be back on the headset by midseason.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Joey Porter Jr. (back) is “considering a second opinion.”
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

Porter Jr. missed training camp and the first two weeks of the regular season with the back issue. His absence was initially believed to be purely related to his contract situation. He lobbied for a new deal all summer and never seemed to make much progress. But the fact that he is seeking additional medical opinions indicates the back issue is real. The Steelers, on the other hand, aren’t buying it. According to Schefter, they are planning for him to potentially play in Week 3. This situation is getting uglier by the week. It’s possible a trade is best for everyone involved. Until some progress is made, the Steelers will continue to be without their top corner.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Keenan Allen “is facing a minimum three-game suspension from the NFL.”
item.description:
Keenan Allen IND Wide Receiver

This stems from Allen’s pair of misdemeanor charges related to a drunk driving arrest that occurred in August. A three-game suspension is the minimum allowed for a DUI or similar arrest under the current collective bargaining agreement. As Schefter notes, the league can make the suspension longer, and Allen’s blood-alcohol content was three times the legal limit. The NFL will wait for the legal process to play out before stepping in with a suspension of its own. That could take several months depending on how things unfold in court.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Puka Nacua (groin) is considered a “pre-game decision” for the Rams’ Week 2 game against the Giants.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Nacua was added to the injury report on Friday as a DNP. He failed to get in any reps on Saturday but still received the questionable designation. Given that the game is on Monday, fantasy managers won’t have many contingency options left. With Jordan Whittington also expected to miss Week 2, the Rams’ No. 2 receiver will be either Konata Mumpfield or Xavier Smith if Nacua doesn’t suit up. Both players would be WR5/6 options in the event of a Nacua absence.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ladd McConkey (rib) is “pushing to play” in Week 2 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

McConkey suffered a cracked rib in the Chargers’ Week 1 loss to the Cardinals. He logged one limited practice this week before being listed as questionable. According to Rapoport, McConkey has “improved more steadily than anticipated.” He notes that the team did not elevate a receiver from the practice squad over the weekend, indicating some optimism that McConkey will play. Fantasy managers will want to check inactives 90 minutes before kickoff, but all signs point to McConkey suiting up today. He will be a high-risk WR2.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports RJ Harvey (hamstring) is “unlikely” to play in Week 2 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
RJ Harvey DEN Running Back

Harvey was listed as limited on Wednesday, though the team didn’t actually hold a practice. They were back on the field for the next two days and listed him as limited. The fact that he practiced in any capacity should mean this isn’t a long-term issue, but the Broncos are playing it safe this week. J.K. Dobbins will see the bulk of the carries and rookie Jonah Coleman could be in line for some of Harvey’s designed touches. Dobbins is locked in as an RB3 for Week 2, while Coleman is more of a deep-cut FLEX play.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jalen McMillan (knee) is expected to play in Week 2 against the Browns, but not in a “full-time role just yet.”
item.description:
Jalen McMillan TB Wide Receiver

The Bucs are going to ease McMillan back into the lineup after he missed Week 1 with the knee injury. McMillan will take rookie Ted Hurst’s spot in the lineup once healthy, but that might not happen until Week 3. Until we see what their split looks like, neither Hurst nor McMillan should be in fantasy lineups.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Kaelon Black (groin) is expected to play in Week 2 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Kaelon Black SF Running Back

Black picked up 14 carries while Christian McCaffrey dealt with cramps in Week 1. Now it’s Black who is banged up, meaning we might get more CMC versus Miami this week. Black was added to the injury report midweek and logged two limited practices before receiving the questionable designation. He is in the RB4 range for Week 2, making him a middling FLEX play.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Chris Olave (hamstring) is expected to play in Week 2 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Chris Olave NO Wide Receiver

Olave left Thursday’s practice as a precaution and was limited again on Friday. The team listed him as questionable heading into the weekend. It seems like the Thursday departure truly was a precaution, and Olave is good to go for a potential shootout with Baltimore. With plenty of passing volume to go around in the Saints’ offense, Olave sits at the end of the WR1 mix for Week 2.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Ravens downgraded WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) to out for Week 2 against the Saints.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

The team pulled the plug on Flowers’ potential to play in Week 2 after the veteran receiver departed the team’s Week 1 win with a hamstring injury. No word yet on how long the injury is expected to sideline Flowers, who appears to have a good shot at suiting up when the team faces off against the Cowboys on the road in Week 3. Tight end Mark Andrews could see a slight uptick in volume in the interim.

item.title: KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson reports Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) could miss two games.
item.description:
Nico Collins HOU Wide Receiver

The Texans received relatively good news from initial testing, which revealed a Grade 1 hamstring injury. Even so, word around the team is that they are preparing to be without their star receiver for two games, which makes sense considering his lengthy soft tissue injury history. Fantasy managers will want to make alternate plans after losing one of their top selections off the board.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Giants CB Deonte Banks (calf) is questionable for Week 2 against the Rams.
item.description:
Deonte Banks NYG Cornerback

Also listed questionable is LB Micah McFadden, while CB Greg Newsome, T Andrew Thomas, DL Chauncey Golston, and OL Francis Mauigoa were removed from the injury report and will play. While Banks’ status is of particular concern against the high-flying Rams aerial attack, their opponent could be without All-Pro wide receiver Puka Nacua, who is listed as questionable with a groin injury.

item.title: Rams WR Puka Nacua (groin) is questionable for Week 2 against the Giants.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Nacua did not practice for the second consecutive day Saturday, prompting the questionable designation for Monday Night Football. The issue is now being called a groin ailment and is reportedly unrelated to the psoas injury he dealt with during the offseason. Fantasy managers will want to start making alternate plans for their first-round pick considering the Rams don’t play until the final game of the week. Jordan Whittington is listed as doubtful with a quad injury.

item.title: Patriots downgraded CB Carlton Davis (neck) to out for Week 2 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Carlton Davis NE Cornerback

Davis was unable to practice all week with a neck injury and will ultimately be held out of the team’s Week 2 game against the Steelers. Pittsburgh will be without starting wide receiver Michael Pittman, so it will be interesting how the Patriots choose to deploy Christian Gonzalez. Gonzalez could find himself in shadow coverage of opposing alpha DK Metcalf.

item.title: Steelers downgraded WR Michael Pittman (foot) to out for Week 2 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

Pittman was unable to get on the practice field this week and will now miss Week 2 as a result of a foot injury. DK Metcalf enters the WR2 discussion in a difficult matchup on paper after ranking in the top five in expected fantasy points in Week 1, for an offense near the top of the league in pass rate over expectation in their first game. Third-year receiver Roman Wilson and rookie Germie Bernard see an uptick in value, although both are difficult starts outside the deepest of leagues. Tight end pat Freiermuth can be started as a back-end TE1 in a pinch.

item.title: Jets placed WR Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

The news was first reported by NFL Insider Ian Rapoport. Cooper is going on injured reserve for an ankle sprain. He’ll be sidelined for at least four games with a designation to return. Rapoport mentions that Cooper should be back “shortly.” Cooper could still make an impact in the second half of his rookie season, but he isn’t worth holding in most fantasy formats at this point.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated believes it’s “worth considering” replacing Lions DC Kelvin Sheppard if Detroit’s defense doesn’t improve.
item.description:
Kelvin Sheppard DET Defensive Coordinator

Appearing on the Rich Eisen Show Friday, Breer was quick to point out the Lions’ defensive struggles. Detroit has allowed 917 yards and 71 points in two games. Breer noted that while the Lions are dealing with injuries in the secondary, that doesn’t excuse their problems in the running game.
