Detroit has allowed 294 rushing yards, 4.8 yards per carry and four rushing touchdowns this year. While it’s still early in the season, Breer says the Lions defensive performance isn’t a “one-off” and that it’s been “messy” for a while. It was a stark contrast from NFL Insider Ian Rapoport’s take on the Pat McAfee show earlier this week where he said, “My guess is the Lions are going to be fine.” Lions HC Dan Campbell has pulled the plug on his offensive coordinator midseason twice in five years, but has afforded his defensive coordinators a longer leash. Sheppard was promoted from linebackers coach to defensive coordinator after Aaron Glenn was hired by the Jets prior to the 2025 season.

Source: The Rich Eisen Show

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “would not be surprised” if Texans WR Jaylin Noel is more involved in Week 2 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Jaylin Noel HOU Wide Receiver

Rapoport adds that Noel is “really talented.” We agree, but the Texans have consistently played WR Xavier Hutchinson ahead of him. Noel, 24, is an explosive player, and the Texans will be looking for playmakers to contribute with WR Nico Collins (hamstring) sidelined this week. Noel is officially on the boom-bust FLEX radar in Week 2 against the Bengals.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Texans WR Kayshon Boutte could be used “a lot” in Week 2 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Kayshon Boutte HOU Wide Receiver

Rapoport’s full quote is winding and hyperbolic, but it sounds like Boutte will be a featured receiver if the Texans believe he is ready to handle that role with WR Nico Collins (hamstring) sidelined. Rapoport notes that Boutte played in “the same” offensive scheme during his time with the Patriots, so adjusting to his new team’s playbook theoretically should have been easy. That said, Boutte caught just one pass last week. He can be treated as a volatile but viable FLEX starter in Week 2.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Giants LT Andrew Thomas (ankle) was limited on Friday.
item.description:
Andrew Thomas NYG Tackle

Giants RG Francis Mauigoa (shoulder) was limited as well. Both offensive linemen are on track to face the Rams in Week 2’s Monday Night Football game, which is good news for QB Jaxson Dart.

Source: Dan Salomone

item.title: Rams WR Jordan Whittington (quad) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Jordan Whittington

Whittington is WR1 Puka Nacua’s direct backup, and Nacua appeared on the injury report today with a hip injury. Neither player practiced. This situation is worth monitoring closely.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) is doubtful for Week 2 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Tua Tagovailoa ATL Quarterback

The Falcons have already named QB Cooper Rush (back) the Week 2 starter. Tagovailoa would only serve as a backup if he is somehow active. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

Source: Atlanta Falcons

item.title: Buccaneers WR Jalen McMillan (knee) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Browns.
item.description:
Jalen McMillan TB Wide Receiver

This is a little surprising. The Buccaneers seem to be taking it very slowly as they bring McMillan back from his knee injury. At this point, he must be treated as being truly questionable to play. He is a boom-bust FLEX if active.

Source: Tampa Bay Buccaneers

item.title: Eagles DT Jalen Carter (wrist) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Titans.
item.description:
Jalen Carter PHI Defensive Tackle

Eagles CB Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) was also cleared to play, though S Andrew Mukuba (knee) is questionable to play after logging a limited session on Friday. The Eagles’ D/ST should have a decent week against the Titans.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: Jaguars WR Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers was limited to two targets last week, but he made the most of them by catching both for 40 yards and one touchdown. The Jaguars face the Broncos’ stout defense this week, but the Jaguars’ ascending passing offense can hold its own. Treat Meyers as a FLEX starter again in Week 2.

Source: Jacksonville Jaguars

item.title: Jaguars WR Brian Thomas (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

Thomas missed a little time in Week 1 after landing on his injured shoulder, but was able to return. The Jaguars’ X-receiver could face Broncos CB Pat Surtain on the perimeter this week, but he should get a few chances to make big plays downfield. He remains a FLEX starter in Week 2.

Source: Jacksonville Jaguars

item.title: Texans ruled out EDGE Jadeveon Clowney (knee) for Week 2 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Jadeveon Clowney HOU Defensive End

Clowney bagged two quarterback pressures and one sack last week. His absence in Week 2 is a plus for Bengals QB Joe Burrow, who logged two limited sessions with back tightness this week before practicing in full.

Source: Houston Texans

item.title: Rams WR Puka Nacua (hip) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

This could be related to the groin and psoas issues Nacua dealt with in August and earlier this month. The Rams’ star wide receiver has an extra day to get this figured out, but it is a tad concerning. For now, make backup plans. It is possible that Nacua is unable to play in Week 2 against the Giants on Monday night. Nacua’s direct backup, WR Jordan Whittington (quad), also missed practice on Friday.

Source: Gary Klein

item.title: Patriots CB Carlton Davis (neck) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Carlton Davis NE Cornerback

Davis did not practice at all this week. He is seemingly a long shot to suit up. The Patriots also listed EDGE Dre’Mont Jones (foot) after three limited practices.

Source: New England Patriots

item.title: Broncos coach Sean Payton said WR Jaylen Waddle “is going to have his touches.”
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Payton was asked if their offseason acquisition, Waddle, was going to be more involved this week than he was in Week 1. Per Payton, they intended to get Waddle more involved, but acknowledged that the team needs to be “more deliberate” about getting him involved, “without forcing it.” The last-second qualifier is a tad unsettling, but we do expect the Broncos to at least look Waddle’s way early, in order to assuage usage concerns. He is a WR2 against the Jaguars this week.

Source: Nick Kosmider

item.title: Rams DT Aaron Donald said he expects to play in Week 2 against the Giants.
item.description:
Aaron Donald

Earlier today, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Donald “hopes” to play on Monday night. A few hours later, Rams coach Sean McVay said he hopes Donald will play this week, but that they need to listen to how Donald is feeling after going through team drills. Donald is evidently feeling good following Friday’s practice and should apparently be expected to face the Giants.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Dolphins Malik Willis (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Malik Willis MIA Quarterback

Willis practiced in full all week, so his toe injury should not be an issue against the 49ers. The Dolphins’ quarterback told reporters this week that he is focused on taking fewer sacks moving forward. As his team fell farther behind on the scoreboard last week, Willis began holding onto the ball for far too long. Getting the ball out quickly or throwing on the run could help.

Source: David Furones

item.title: 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Kittle will likely remain on a snap count in Week 2, though his usage should continue steadily ticking upward. He can be started as a TE1 against the Dolphins’ fantasy-friendly defense this week.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Chargers DT Teair Tart (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Teair Tart LAC Defensive Lineman

Tart is good to go for his team’s Week 2 game against a division rival. The Chargers will, however, be without DB Elijah Molden (hamstring).

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Cardinals TE Trey McBride (rest/back) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Trey McBride ARI Tight End

McBride is good to go for the Cardinals’ matchup against the Seahawks and can be treated as a shoo-in TE1, per usual. The Seahawks are without S Ty Okada (hamstring), theoretically making life a little easier for McBride. Fellow S Nick Emmanwori (hip/ankle) is questionable.

Source: Arizona Cardinals

item.title: 49ers K Eddy Pineiro (illness) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Eddy Pineiro SF Kicker

According to ESPN’s Nick Wagoner, the 49ers will sign a kicker to the practice squad as insurance, in case Pineiro cannot play. This is unfortunate. The 49ers’ starting kicker should bank a decent number of extra points, and ideally field goals, against the Dolphins this week.

Source: ESPN

item.title: 49ers RB Kaelon Black (groin) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Kaelon Black SF Running Back

Black appeared on the 49ers’ injury report yesterday as a limited participant. He was seen practicing today during the portion of practice open to the media, but we do not know if he managed to practice in full. If so, that would be encouraging. The 49ers face the Dolphins’ unimposing defense this weekend. If Black is active, he can be started in FLEX spots, though ideally we get an update on his health beforehand.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: Broncos ruled out WR Marvin Mims (foot) for Week 2 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Marvin Mims DEN Wide Receiver

It sure seems like Mims aggravated his preexisting foot injury in Week 1 against the Chiefs. Mims does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues, though his absence does slightly improve the rest of the receiving corps’ outlook.

Source: Parker J. Gabriel

item.title: Broncos RB RJ Harvey (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
RJ Harvey DEN Running Back

Even if Harvey is active, he makes for a dicey FLEX start. The second-year running back totaled seven touches in last week’s loss and he logged only two limited practices this week. The Broncos can divvy up the backfield work between RB J.K. Dobbins, Harvey and rookie RB Jonah Coleman if need be.

Source: Parker J. Gabriel

item.title: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Colts.
item.description:
Patrick Mahomes KC Quarterback

Mahomes ran the ball seven times for 23 yards and one touchdown last week before practicing in full this week. Both factors are encouraging. The Chiefs’ star quarterback warrants QB1 treatment against the Colts in Week 2.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Colts.
item.description:
Rashee Rice KC Wide Receiver

Rice earned only two targets in Week 1, yet still technically warrants WR2 treatment based on his theoretical role in the offense, along with his past WR1 performances. The Chiefs notably faced the Broncos’ top-tier defense last week and will get a far softer matchup against the Colts in Week 2.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Seahawks WR Tory Horton (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Tory Horton SEA Wide Receiver

Horton’s return boosts QB Drew Lock’s passing outlook, though Horton is not worth starting in 12-team FLEX spots, operating in the Seahawks WR4 role.

Source: Seattle Seahawks

item.title: Chiefs DT Chris Jones (calf) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Colts.
item.description:
Chris Jones KC Defensive Tackle

Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane (shoulder) is also questionable to play this week, though Chiefs coach Andy Reid said earlier this week “there’s a pretty good chance” Delane will suit up in Week 1. Jones remained limited all week. Delane logged two full sessions before downgrading to limited on Friday, which could indicate he suffered a setback. We will find out soon enough.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Chiefs ruled out LT Josh Simmons (back) for Week 2 against the Colts.
item.description:
Josh Simmons KC Tackle

Backup OT Kahlil Benson will start in Simmons’ stead. He did so last week and avoided major mistakes. The Chiefs also ruled out CB Chamarri Conner (knee).

Source: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk

item.title: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle/hip) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Nick Emmanwori SEA Safety

Emmanwori picked up a hip injury mid-week. Hopefully, he is good to go by Sunday. The Seahawks ruled out fellow starting S Ty Okada (hamstring) for this one, but the Seahawks D/ST remains formidable overall.

item.title: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (ribs) is questionable for Week 2 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

McConkey managed a limited session Friday and eventually drew the questionable tag as he attempts to play through a rib injury suffered in Week 1. Considering his value to this team, we would expect him to do what he can to play. That said, fantasy managers find themselves in a pickle with the Chargers not playing until the afternoon portion of games, meaning alternate plans should be in the works over the weekend. McConkey is a locked-in WR2 with WR1 upside, if active.

item.title: Commanders WR Jaylin Lane (groin) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Jaylin Lane WAS Wide Receiver

Lane caught 1-of-1 targets for four yards last week. He is not on the fantasy radar for 12-team managed leagues, although it is nice to know that his groin is feeling better. Commanders rookie WR Antonio Williams has seemingly leapfrogged Lane after one game.

Source: Ben Standig

item.title: Commanders RB Kaytron Allen (knee/ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Kaytron Allen WAS Running Back

Allen practiced in full all week, so there are no concerns about his current status. Last week, starting RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt fumbled late in the game and was yanked for the final eight plays. Last Man Standig’s Ben Standig notes, Allen “handled the final three handoffs, and Rachaad White was a potential safety valve” for the Commanders’ two-point attempt. Allen is worth stashing on benches in 12-team leagues.

Source: Last Man Standig

item.title: Nico Collins (hamstring) has been ruled out for Week 2 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Nico Collins HOU Wide Receiver

Collins was added to the injury report on Thursday and will miss Week 2 with yet another soft tissue injury. Considering his lengthy history of hamstring issues, we would not be surprised if this turned into a multi-game absence for the talented alpha. Expect Kayshon Boutte to see an uptick in routes, while it is likely Xavier Hutchinson kicks to the perimeter to make room for Jaylin Noel in the slot. Collins’ absence benefits veteran tight end Dalton Schultz the most, whom enters the TE1 ranks in a matchup made in heaven against the inside-funnel Bengals.

item.title: Bengals QB Joe Burrow (back) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Texans.
item.description:
Joe Burrow CIN Quarterback

This listing is effectively a formality. Burrow laughed off the idea of missing the Bengals’ game against the Texans earlier this week, and today, coach Zac Taylor said Burrow is “good to go” after practicing in full. Burrow’s status is, of course, worth following, but we do expect him to play. Treat him as a QB1, per usual.

Source: Paul Dehner Jr.

item.title: Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

Pierce’s Thursday absence appears to have been a rest day. The Colts reportedly plan to play Pierce more in Week 2 than they did in Week 1, when he played on 59 percent of the team’s snaps. He posted a 4/61 receiving line and can be viewed as a WR3/FLEX this week.

Source: Indianapolis Colts

item.title: Eagles EDGE Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) is out for Week 2 against the Titans.
item.description:
Jonathan Greenard PHI EDGE

Greenard will miss his second straight game to start his first season in Philadelphia. He managed a week of limited sessions, seemingly indicating he is inching closer to being available after being acquired this offseason.

item.title: Steelers ruled out CB Joey Porter (back/contract) for Week 2 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reported earlier today that the Steelers and Porter are at an impasse over the guaranteed money the Steelers are offering as the two sides attempt to agree on an extension. The Steelers typically do not guarantee any money beyond the deal’s first year. Porter, obviously, takes issue with that policy. He also seemingly has a back injury. According to Pryor, Porter’s relationship with the team may be damaged beyond repair.

Source: Brooke Pryor

item.title: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play against the Steelers.
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

Henderson logged a complete week of full practices after missing Week 1 with the ankle injury, returning to the fold to join Rhamondre Stevenson as the top two rushers for the Patriots. The fact that he was able to practice in full for three straight days seems to indicate there won’t be any restrictions with his workload, meaning fantasy managers can start him as a viable FLEX option against the Steelers.

item.title: Steelers WR Michael Pittman (foot) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

Pittman did not practice at all this week. If he plays, he could be fairly limited. We tentatively expect him to be inactive on game day, though. Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth had a solid role last week and could take on No. 2 pass-catcher duties if Pittman indeed cannot play. Steelers WR DK Metcalf will almost assuredly take on a larger role, operating as the team’s receiving focal point.

Source: Brooke Pryor

item.title: Ravens OLB Trey Hendrickson (finger) is questionable for Week 2 against the Saints.
item.description:
Trey Hendrickson BAL Outside Linebacker

Hendrickson managed to upgrade to a limited showing in practice Friday after missing the previous two days, opening the door for him to be active on Sunday. The perennial tradition of the Ravens experiencing significant defensive injuries seems to be making an appearance early this year, with Nnamdi Madubuike and T.J. Tampa already ruled out.

item.title: Ravens LT Ronnie Stanley (toe) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Saints.
item.description:
Ronnie Stanley BAL Tackle

Stanley and LG John Simpson (groin) both resumed practicing on Friday, though only via limited sessions. The left-side duo is firmly in the questionable column. If inactive, their losses could be somewhat consequential, though Saints EDGE Chase Young (calf) is also questionable to play.

Source: Jonas Shaffer

item.title: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) is doubtful to play in Week 2 against the Saints.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Flowers entered the season at the tail end of a rehab program for the hamstring strain he suffered on August 31st. He logged two full practice sessions before dominating the Colts early on in Week 1. Unfortunately, Flowers balled too hard, aggravating the hamstring injury in the process. He is unlikely to play this week, but his return to practice today is a great sign for his Week 3 availability. The Ravens placed WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) on injured reserve this week. This means WRs Rashod Bateman, Elijah Sarratt and Devontez Walker could be asked to step up, although TE Mark Andrews will probably serve as the team’s top pass-catching option.

Source: Jonas Shaffer

item.title: Bears RT Darnell Wright (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Darnell Wright CHI Offensive Lineman

Wright is good to go against the Vikings’ blitz-happy defense. Bears OT Ozzy Trapilo (knee) was also removed from the injury report, though it is unclear whether he will actually make his 2026 debut. The second-year offensive lineman’s promising rookie season was cut short by a ruptured patellar tendon. He was listed as questionable last week before being ruled out. If active, he would likely serve as a backup, but this is great news overall.

Source: Dan Wiederer

item.title: Bears RB D’Andre Swift (ankle, knee) and Kyle Monangai (hamstring) were removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Vikings.
item.description:
D'Andre Swift CHI Running Back

Both backs saw their practice reps monitored this week as they dealt with normal wear-and-tear, ultimately removed from the injury report Friday. Both will play against the Vikings in a divisional showdown after contributing to the league’s top rushing attack in Week 1. Fantasy managers can start Swift as a back-end RB1 and Monangai as a viable FLEX.

item.title: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said he expects rookie RB Demond Claiborne to be active for Week 2 against the Bears.
item.description:
Demond Claiborne MIN Running Back

According to ESPN’s Kevin Seifert, Claiborne and RB DeeJay Dallas will also be “part of the group” that backs up starting RB Aaron Jones with RB Jordan Mason (thumb) on injured reserve. Dallas was active last week, while the team kept Claiborne, the rookie, inactive, so it stands to reason that Dallas could play more snaps than Claiborne. That said, some beat reporters viewed Claiborne favorably this summer. He can be stashed on benches in 12-team leagues to see how things shake out.

Source: Kevin Seifert

item.title: Vikings WR Jauan Jennings (personal) is out for Week 2 against the Bears.
item.description:
Jauan Jennings MIN Wide Receiver

Head coach Kevin O’Connell ruled out veteran receiver Jauan Jennings, citing a death of a close family member. Jennings will step away from the team to mourn the passing, leaving Tai Felton as the player most likely to step into his vacated role when the Vikings take on the Bears. Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison should take on all the volume they can handle with the team also without Jordan Mason. Jefferson is a locked-in WR1 while Addison offers an intriguing upside-WR2 profile after putting up a dud in Week 1.

item.title: Minnesota Vikings QB Carson Wentz will start in Week 2 against the Bears.
item.description:
Carson Wentz MIN Quarterback

Wentz played serviceably last week after starting QB Kyler Murray suffered a concussion. The Bears’ pass defense looks like a unit worth targeting in fantasy. Wentz can be viewed as a QB2 with decent upside, though only WR Justin Jefferson can be viewed as the clear-cut safe fantasy starter.

Source: Brad Biggs

item.title: Raiders TE Brock Bowers (knee) is doubtful for Week 2 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Bowers returned to the practice field Friday but apparently needs more time before he returns from his meniscectomy surgery performed less than two weeks ago. Michael Mayer will once again serve as the primary tight end after ranking second on the team in route rate while leading the team in targets (seven) against the Dolphins in Week 1. Continue to start Mayer as a locked-in TE1 for as long as Bowers remains sidelined.

item.title: Vikings ruled out QB Kyler Murray (concussion) for Week 2 against the Bears.
item.description:
Kyler Murray MIN Quarterback

Reports regarding Murray’s progress in the NFL’s concussion protocol were positive this week, but it looks like he needs another week to fully recover. The Vikings will instead roll QB Carson Wentz as the starter in what could be a high-scoring game against the Bears. He is a QB2 for the occasion.

Source: Brad Biggs

item.title: Rams S Kamren Kinchens (hamstring) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Kamren Kinchens

This is Kinchens’ second missed practice. Fellow Rams S Kam Curl (ankle) has now logged two limited sessions and should be good to go, but the team’s safety unit is ailing. They typically use three-safety looks, with DB Quentin Lake doubling as a safety and nickel coverage defender. The Rams signed S Tanner Ingle from the practice squad to the active roster. The Rams face the Giants on Monday night.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Saints DE Cam Jordan (hamstring) was removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 2 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Cameron Jordan NO Defensive End

Jordan will make his season debut after missing the team’s Week 1 game against the Lions. Long snapper Zach Wood was ruled out after being added to the injury report Thursday with a calf injury.

item.title: Saints TE Juwan Johnson (illness) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Juwan Johnson NO Tight End

Johnson posted a 3/54/1 receiving line last week and can be treated as a TE1 again in Week 2. Saints WR1 Chris Olave is nursing a hamstring strain, though the team is telling reporters that the injury is not concerning. Johnson could take on a slightly larger workload if Olave is at all limited, though we won’t know if that is the case until the dust settles and the game ends.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Saints placed LS Zach Wood on injured reserve with a calf injury.
item.description:
Zach Wood NO Long Snapper

Wood was diagnosed with a Grade 2 calf strain earlier this week. He is expected to miss 4-6 weeks.

Source: Kat Terrell

item.title: Saints RB Alvin Kamara (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

Kamara has successfully rehabbed his MCL sprain and resumed practicing in full this week. He joins a Saints backfield that employed a committee approach in Week 1. Kamara should be expected to play on passing downs. Whether he takes a meaningful rushing share and rotates in for red zone snaps remains unknown. He warrants PPR FLEX consideration with RB2 upside.

Source: Ari Meirov

item.title: Saints WR Chris Olave (hamstring) is questionable for Week 2 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Chris Olave NO Wide Receiver

Olave was present at the portion of practice available to media Friday after being limited for “precautionary reasons” the day prior. Although he seems to be trending towards playing against the Ravens, the questionable designation is something fantasy managers will want to monitor when game-day inactives are announced 90-minutes prior to first kick. The good news is that the Saints play in the early window on Sunday, giving managers time to react should they be dealt a surprise on Sunday. Olave will be a volume-driven WR1 against the Ravens, if active.

item.title: Saints EDGE Chase Young (calf) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Chase Young NO Defensive End

Young experienced “some soreness in his calf” during practice on Thursday, resulting in a limited session. New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett notes that Young was practicing during the portion of practice available to the media on Friday, and he was told Young’s early exit on Thursday was “more precautionary” than a significant concern. A calf injury kept Young sidelined for multiple games last year. It sounds like he has a chance to play this week, but it’s possible the team could limit his snaps.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur reiterated that Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier are “gonna rotate” this season.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

LaFleur is again insisting that Love, the No. 3 overall pick of this year’s draft, and 2026 free agent signee Allgeier will rotate in the backfield, while adding that it “is a long season.” Love saw 13 touches in last week’s win over the Chargers, while Allgeier had 19, and was out-snapped by Allgeier 41 to 32. A similar rotation going forward would put a damper on Love’s week-to-week upside after the rookie spent most of the offseason going as a top-30 pick in fantasy drafts, but he’ll maintain a decent value as long as he continues to see double-digit touches. Both Love and Allgeier will be hard to trust as anything more than fringe RB2/RB3 this week against the Seahawks.

Source: Theo Mackie

item.title: Teven Jenkins (back) will not play in Week 2 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Teven Jenkins CLE Guard

Jenkins will miss a second straight game with a back injury that has sidelined him since last Thursday’s practice. The sixth-year guard was replaced by Austin Barber in last week’s game against the Jaguars. Barber appeared on 51 snaps, earning a PFF grade of 82.6 while allowing just one QB pressure on 33 pass-blocking snaps.

item.title: Browns CB Tyson Campbell (concussion) is questionable for Week 2 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Tyson Campbell CLE Cornerback

Campbell departed the team’s Week 1 loss to the Jaguars with a head injury and was placed in the league’s concussion protocol. He was unable to practice in any capacity Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to limited Friday, at least keeping the door open for a potential return to the active roster. Even so, recent trends indicate he is more likely to miss Week 2 considering over two-thirds of players to enter the protocol miss at least one game.

item.title: Falcons QB Cooper Rush will start in Week 2 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Cooper Rush ATL Quarterback

It was reported earlier that Rush was expected to draw the start, but with Michael Penix Jr. (knee) officially ruled out, it will be Rush getting the ball against the Panthers. Rush struggled in last week’s game against the Steelers, throwing for 143 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions on 22 attempts. Drake London shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a WR2 in fantasy this week with Rush under center, while Kyle Pitts profiles as a boom-or-bust TE1 after putting up zero fantasy points in Week 1. Jack Strand will serve as Rush’s backup.

Source: Atlanta Falcons

item.title: Falcons ruled out QB Michael Penix Jr. (knee) for Week 2 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Michael Penix ATL Quarterback

Cooper Rush will draw a second consecutive start under center and will be backed up by undrafted free agent rookie Jack Strand, with Tua Tagovailoa not yet ready to return from an oblique injury. Penix is expected to enter the starting lineup once cleared to return to game action as he continues his ramp-up process following a torn ACL suffered in 2025.

item.title: Rams DT Aaron Donald said he expects to play in Week 2 against the Giants.
item.description:
Aaron Donald

Earlier today, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Donald “hopes” to play on Monday night. A few hours later, Rams coach Sean McVay said he hoped Donald would play this week, but that they need to listen to how Donald was feeling after going through team drills. Donald is evidently feeling good following Friday’s practice and should apparently be expected to face the Giants.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) will play in Week 2 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

Coker was removed from the Panthers’ final injury report on Friday after logging a full practice to close out the week. Coker was spotted in a walking boot at the start of the week, but downplayed any concern about his injury, saying he rolled his ankle “a little bit” but expected to play against the Falcons. The 24-year-old receiver turned in an impressive 8-138-2 performance on nine targets last week against the Bears and can be viewed as a fringe WR2/WR3 this week.

Source: Carolina Panthers

item.title: Raiders TE Brock Bowers (knee) returned to practice Friday.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

The team has yet to release an official injury designation for the talented tight end, but his return to the practice field leaves the door open for a potential return to the game-day roster. Head coach Klint Kubiak continues to be adamant that Bowers would not miss extended time, something that seemed ridiculous throughout the week but now gains traction with Bowers returning to practice. Fantasy managers will want to wait until an official designation is passed by the team before solidifying their plans for Week 2. Bowers would immediately return to a top-tier TE1 against the Chargers, if active.

item.title: Colts HC Shane Steichen said Anthony Richardson (groin) will be good to go for Week 2 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Anthony Richardson IND Quarterback

Richardson will be dressed to back up Daniel Jones in Sunday’s game against the Chiefs. Richardson tweaked his groin while lifting earlier this week, per head coach Shane Steichen, but he is good to go.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Panthers WR Jalen Coker (ankle) was a full participant in practice Friday.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

We’re still waiting on his official game designation, but the upgrade to a full session Friday reinforces previous reports that Coker would be good to go in Week 2 against the Falcons. Fresh off a career game in Week 1, Coker can be safely inserted into fantasy rosters as an upside WR3 in a matchup with a Falcons team with no shortage of injuries on the defensive side of the ball. Defensive tackle Bobby Brown was absent again and was ruled out for Week 2.

item.title: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) will not play in Week 2 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

Okonkwo did not log a practice this week after suffering a hamstring injury in the second half of last week’s game against the Eagles. His absence will leave the Commanders noticeably thin at tight end as far as pass-catchers are concerned, as the next man up on the depth chart is blocking TE John Bates, followed by third-year TE Ben Sinnott, who could see an uptick in the passing game after running 10 routes in Week 1. Fantasy managers should avoid this tight end room altogether despite a plus matchup against the Cowboys. In addition to Okonkwo, the Commanders have also ruled out LB Frankie Luvu (groin).

Source: John Keim

item.title: Joe Burrow (back tightness) will play in Week 2 against the Texans.
item.description:
Joe Burrow CIN Quarterback

Burrow was upgraded to a full participant in Friday’s practice and is good to go for Sunday’s game, per head coach Zac Taylor. Burrow was limited in the first two practices of the week due to back tightness, but that was likely more out of precaution than it was due to anything serious. Burrow profiles as a high-end QB1 against the Texans.

Source: Ben Baby

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cooper Rush is expected to start in Week 2 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Cooper Rush ATL Quarterback

Rush is taking all of the first-team reps with the Falcons in Friday’s practice, and according to Rapoport, sources familiar with the situation expect Rush to get the nod on Sunday. With Rush under center, all Falcons pass-catchers receive a substantial downgrade after he struggled to move the ball in Week 1 against the Steelers. Fantasy managers hoping Drake London and Kyle Pitts can be of some value against a Panthers defense that allowed 269 yards and two passing TDs to the Bears last week should approach both players with caution. London is best trusted as more of a WR2, while Pitts, who saw one target on 21 routes last week, shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 in what figures to be a run-heavy game for the Falcons.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Zay Flowers (hamstring) returned to practice on Friday.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Flowers missed back-to-back practices to start the week, but his return on Friday is an encouraging sign for him entering the weekend. The Ravens will release their final injury report shortly, but it wouldn’t be surprising if Flowers drew a questionable tag and was viewed as a game-day decision after the Ravens have a chance to look at him in warmups. We will provide an update on his status when we learn more.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: Nico Collins (hamstring) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Nico Collins HOU Wide Receiver

Collins has missed each of the Texans’ last two practices and is at risk of being sidelined for Week 2’s game against the Bengals. The team will release its final injury report later in the day, but the timing of his injury, coupled with back-to-back DNPs, doesn’t bode well for Collins this weekend. If he were to miss Sunday’s game, Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte would be on the radar as potential dart throws in deeper leagues.

Source: Jonathan M Alexander

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Josh Jacobs could be facing a 4-6 game suspension after he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

The league is reportedly pushing to get hold of the videotaped incident that took place between Jacobs and his ex-girlfriend, but the victim has filed a motion that states the disclosure of the tape would threaten her “privacy, dignity, security, and emotional well-being.” Fowler says this motion will make acquiring the tape “increasingly harder for the league,” but that a four-to-six-game suspension is believed to be in range for Jacobs, according to people Fowler has spoken with across the league. Jacobs remains on the commissioner’s exempt list and will not be active for Week 2’s game against the Jets.

Source: ESPN

item.title: ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reports a source familiar with Joey Porter’s (back/contract) situation said “I don’t know if he ever puts on a Steelers uniform again.”
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

According to Pryor, the Steelers’ relationship with Porter “may be fractured beyond repair.” The fourth-year corner has been seeking a contract extension all offseason and missed Week 1 with a back injury that some believe could improve with a new deal. Porter logged a full practice on Wednesday only to reaggravate it on Thursday, putting his Week 2 availability in doubt. According to Pryor, one major holdup in a deal between Porter and the Steelers is the lack of guaranteed money the Steelers are willing to give him. The Steelers typically don’t give out guaranteed money beyond the first year of a deal, but made an exception for T.J. Watt on his extension. Porter reportedly hoped for a similar exception, but so far, that hasn’t happened. This situation remains far from resolved. With Friday’s practice still to go, we’ll see if Porter is ruled in/out before the weekend or if his status will be one to look out for closer to game day.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said he “fully anticipates” more snaps for LeQuin Allen on third down.
item.description:
LeQuint Allen

Allen played on just one offensive snap in last week’s win over the Browns, but led the Jaguars in third-down snaps (146) last season. Despite all the snaps he saw on third down as a rookie, Allen never materialized into a viable fantasy option. Whether or not that changes this season is to be determined, but any additional snaps he receives on third down would come at the expense of Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, after Rodriguez led the way with five third-down snaps last week. While Allen seeing additional work in these situations could be problematic for fantasy managers, they shouldn’t let that deter them from starting Tuten in Week 2 against the Broncos.

Source: Ryan O’Halloran

item.title: Keon Coleman caught all six targets for 63 yards in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions.
item.description:
Keon Coleman BUF Wide Receiver

Coleman could be a hot name on the waiver wire following Week 2 after DJ Moore departed with what appeared to be a significant shoulder injury in the first half. The third-year veteran continues to tease at untapped upside in this high-powered offense but has yet to fully break through for consistent production. Maybe that changes now as his role potentially grows without Moore. It will also be interesting to see how, if at all, his route tree changes in the absence of Moore, particularly considering the team has Joshua Palmer to operate as the field-stretching, Z-type receiver, the latter of whom caught his only target for a 43-yard touchdown on a broken coverage against the Lions. Coleman is a speculative waiver addition ahead of a much more forgiving matchup against the Jets in Week 3.

item.title: Dalton Kincaid caught 7-of-8 targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Kincaid truly did it all in this one, routinely in the middle of the blocking scrum on long James Cook runs in addition to his work through the air. His 95 yards handily paced the team, with his first touchdown of the young season coming from 16 yards out near the end of the second quarter. Kincaid remains one of the most efficient pass-catchers in the league on a per-route basis and has worked his way into the upper echelon of fantasy assets at the position. He remains a locked-in TE1 when the Bills host the Jets in Week 3.

item.title: James Cook rushed 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions, adding four yards on one reception.
item.description:
James Cook BUF Running Back

Cook jumped out to a scorching start on the ground, reaching the century mark in rushing before the half. Still, fantasy managers were left scratching their head as they watched Josh Allen account for three touchdowns from inside the five, two on the ground and one through the air. It wasn’t until a 22-yard carry that was down at the one late in the fourth quarter that the team rewarded Cook with a short-yardage touchdown, finally allowing fantasy managers their first taste of sweet touchdown copium from their first-round draft pick on the young season. Cook is likely to remain busy when the Bills host the Jets in Week 3, where he will remain a locked-in RB1.

item.title: Josh Allen completed 20-of-31 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns in the Bills’ 41-31, Week 2 win over the Lions, adding 69 yard and two touchdowns on 14 carries.
item.description:
Josh Allen BUF Quarterback

Was it ever a doubt that Super Josh would make an appearance in the franchise’s first game in their new stadium? To the utter dismay of James Cook fantasy managers, Allen accounted for three touchdowns from inside the five against the Lions, two with his legs and one with his arm, extending his NFL-record for games with multiple rushing touchdowns and multiple passing touchdowns to 10 in the process. The unquestioned overall QB1 in fantasy circles continues to prove the doubters wrong as the Bills surge to 2-0 atop the AFC ahead of a home meeting with the Chargers in Week 3. Allen remains a top-tier fantasy asset until pigs fly.

item.title: Jameson Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 33 yards in the Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Jameson Williams DET Wide Receiver

Williams continues to be primarily utilized as a deep threat in the Detroit offense, which is not the development fantasy managers were expecting following offseason reports that his route tree would be expanded in the new year. The mounting injuries along the offensive line have limited Goff’s time in the pocket to the point where Williams rarely has enough time for his routes to develop, leading to the down production through two weeks. Whether either of those two variables changes in the immediate future remains to be seen, leaving us to treat Williams as nothing more than an upside WR3 in the interim. He will be a difficult start in Week 3 when the Lions host the Jets.

item.title: Sam LaPorta caught 6-of-7 targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

LaPorta combined with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs to be the primary targets for quarterback Jared Goff on a night where relentless pressure from the Bills forced the offense to primarily attack the intermediate areas of the field. That could be the norm for this offense moving forward considering the mounting injuries along their offensive line, which are likely to be felt the most against opponents with a legitimate pass rush. That may not be the case in Week 3 when the Lions host the Jets, a team that is likely to also utilize elevated rates of zone coverage. LaPorta has had stark man-zone splits throughout his career and could see less volume due to matchup. He’ll be a low-end TE1 against the Jets.

item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 9-of-13 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Amon-Ra St. Brown DET Wide Receiver

St. Brown did not catch his first pass until six minutes left in the second quarter but was the primary cog of the offense after the break as the Lions worked to overcome multiple 17-point deficits. He found paint for the first time on the team’s first possession after the break before adding a second in the two-minute drill from 27 yards out. St. Brown now has 209 yards and four touchdowns on 19 receptions through two games an looks every bit of the elite WR1 fantasy managers invested a first-round pick into this offseason. Although volume through the air might be more difficult to come by in Week 3, St. Brown remains a top-tier WR1 when the Lions host the Jets in Detroit.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 16 times for 52 yards in the Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Bills, adding 61 yards and a touchdown on six receptions.
item.description:
Jahmyr Gibbs DET Running Back

Gibbs was effectively the entire game plan out of the gates, scoring the team’s only first-half touchdown from 11 yards out in the second quarter. He would be used far less after the break as the Lions attempted to come back from multiple 17-point deficits, although the six receptions on eight targets and a touchdown through the air helped push his counting stats into clear RB1 territory for the second consecutive week to start the season. Fantasy managers that were lucky enough to secure the 1.01 in drafts this offseason are sure to be content with the early returns. Gibbs will once again be an elite fantasy option when the Lions host the Jets in Week 3.

item.title: Jared Goff completed 26-of-38 passes for 327 yards and four touchdowns in the Lions’ 41-31, Week 2 loss to the Bills, adding seven yards on three carries.
item.description:
Jared Goff DET Quarterback

The Lions staked the Bills to a 21-point lead early in the second quarter, eventually taking a 27-10 deficit into the break. The closest they would get the rest of the game was a 10-point deficit, but the offense finally came alive in the final two frames. Goff tossed a pair of touchdowns to alpha wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and one each to Sam LaPorta and Jahmyr Gibbs, salvaging the poor team performance with an elite fantasy score for managers brave enough to start him on the road in the elements. The Lions fall to 1-1 ahead of a much more forgiving home matchup against the Jets in Week 3, where Goff will look to return another QB1 performance.

item.title: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) went to the locker room early ahead of the half in Week 2 against the Lions.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

Moore departed with just over three minutes remaining in the second quarter after appearing to injure his shoulder on a diving attempt in the end zone. He remained on the field for multiple minutes before being helped to the sideline with trainers. He went straight to the locker room under his own power, presumably for testing. The team has yet to release an official designation, although it appears unlikely he will return to the game. Moore was not targeted before departing as the play he was injured on was called back for an offensive hold.

item.title: Lions DB Avonte Maddox (undisclosed) was carted to the locker room in the second quarter of Week 2 against the Bills.
item.description:
Avonte Maddox DET Defensive Back

Maddox was injured on a play in the red zone at the beginning of the second quarter. He was helped to the sideline by trainers before being taken by cart to the locker room. Expect an update from the team in short order. His departure is another blow to a secondary already down multiple starters.

item.title: Giants LT Andrew Thomas (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Andrew Thomas NYG Tackle

Thomas and RG Francis Mauigoa (shoulder) are both practicing in a limited capacity, putting them on track to play on Monday night against the Rams. There are no concerns here.

Source: Sarah Barshop

item.title: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle/hip) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Nick Emmanwori SEA Safety

Emmanwori remains limited through two Week 2 practices, and Okada (hamstring) has not yet resumed practicing. Emmanwori seemingly has a chance to play, but Okada appears to be a long shot.

Source: Bob Condotta

item.title: The Athletic’s Chad Graff believes getting WR Kyle Williams more involved will help the Patriots generate explosive plays.
item.description:
Kyle Williams NE Wide Receiver

The issue is that Williams “didn’t display much craftiness in his route running during training camp this summer.” He ended up “buried on the depth chart” and played just 12 snaps in the opener. Still, Graff notes, Williams has shown an ability to “release off the line of scrimmage with ease, and run straight, deep routes for big completions.” Getting Williams more involved makes sense, but the Patriots have been reluctant to do so thus far in his career. He can be stashed on deep-leagues benches for a week or so, but positive results are not guaranteed.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: 49ers K Eddy Pineiro (illness) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Eddy Pineiro SF Kicker

NFL players generally play through illnesses. We expect Pineiro to be active on game day, though two absences are a bit concerning. Hopefully, he is back on Friday.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Kittle’s continued limited participation is not concerning. The 49ers are likely just managing the veteran’s reps early in the year, coming off a season-ending injury. Kittle is a TE1 for the 49ers’ Week 2 game against the Dolphins.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: 49ers RB Kaelon Black (groin) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
item.description:
Kaelon Black SF Running Back

Black gets tagged with the dreaded mid-week limited listing. Dang. The rookie running back was a helpful contributor in Week 1, elevating him to FLEX-starter status for the 49ers’ matchup against the Dolphins’ fantasy-friendly defense in Week 2. He is now in the questionable camp, though. Hopefully, he practices fully on Friday.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: Jaguars WR Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers should be good to go for his team’s Week 2 game against the Broncos. He caught 2-of-2 targets for 40 yards and one touchdown in Week 1 against the Browns, and can be expected to play efficiently again in Week 2, albeit on a potentially stunted workload. The Jaguars field a deep wide receiver corps. Jaguars RB LeQuint Allen (hip) remained limited as well.

Source: Demetrius Harvey

item.title: Jaguars WR Brian Thomas (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

The Jaguars are seemingly just managing Thomas’ reps after their X-receiver aggravated his shoulder injury in Week 1 against the Browns. Thomas remains a volatile WR3/FLEX playing in a productive, if crowded, offense.

Source: Demetrius Harvey

item.title: Eagles DT Jalen Carter (wrist) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Jalen Carter PHI Defensive Tackle

Eagles CB Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) and OLB Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) joined Carter for a limited session. Eagles S Andrew Mukuba (knee) did not practice. Fortunately, the Eagles have a winnable game against the Titans this week.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: Broncos WR Marvin Mims (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Marvin Mims DEN Wide Receiver

Mims seems to have aggravated the foot injury he suffered in the Broncos’ preseason finale. He practiced fully last week, but has not taken the field since Monday night’s loss to the Chiefs. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

Source: Parker J. Gabriel

item.title: Broncos RB RJ Harvey (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
RJ Harvey DEN Running Back

Harvey joined his teammates on the field for a limited session after sitting out on Wednesday. He has a chance to play. If active, it is unclear how effective he can be, and the Broncos do have a capable backup, rookie RB Jonah Coleman, who should be stashed where available. Hopefully, Harvey practices fully tomorrow. Stay tuned.

Source: Parker J. Gabriel

item.title: Vikings QB Kyler Murray (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Kyler Murray MIN Quarterback

Murray logs his second limited session of the week. He has a chance to play, but we simply will not know his status until the team announces that he has passed the NFL’s concussion protocol. If Vikings QB2 Carson Wentz gets the start against the Bears, he would be a worthwhile QB2 in fantasy.

Source: Sean Hammond

item.title: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said Will McDonald will play in Week 2 against the Packers.
item.description:
Will McDonald NYJ Defensive End

McDonald popped up on Thursday’s injury report with an ankle injury, but speaking with the media on Friday, Glenn said the fourth-year pass rusher will be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Packers. Rookie CB D’Angelo Ponds, who missed last week with an ankle injury, is also expected to make his NFL debut this week, giving the Jets additional help in the secondary.

Source: Zack Rosenblatt

item.title: Omar Cooper (ankle) will not play in Week 2 against the Packers.
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

This was always expected to be the case, but head coach Aaron Glenn said on Friday, while speaking with the media, that Cooper, RB/KR Kene Nwangwu (back), S Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin), and EDGE Joseph Ossai (foot) will all miss Sunday’s game against the Packers. It was reported earlier this week that the Jets are hoping to have Cooper back “within the next four weeks,” so it wouldn’t be surprising if he also missed Week 3’s game against the Lions.

Source: Zack Rosenblatt

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Aaron Donald “hopes” to play in Week 2 against the Giants.
item.description:
Aaron Donald

Donald was reportedly close to being ready for the Rams’ season opener in Australia, but now the future Hall of Famer hopes to return in the Rams’ official home opener on Monday Night Football against the Giants. While Donald playing in Week 2 is still not a sure thing, he logged a full practice Thursday, which is a good sign with one practice still to go this week.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Bengals expect Joe Burrow (back tightness) to play in Week 2 against the Texans.
item.description:
Joe Burrow CIN Quarterback

Burrow has been limited in each of the team’s first two practices, likely because the Bengals are exercising caution with their QB1. With one more practice to go before the Bengals release their final injury report, it sounds like there is no real concern about Burrow’s availability for Week 2 against a Texans defense looking to rebound from a tough season opener in which they allowed 36 points to the Bills. We will be sure to provide a final status for Burrow once the team announces it.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports DJ Moore (shoulder) is “not a lock” to play in Week 3 against the Chargers.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

This is already shaping up to be an injury that will be monitored throughout all of next week. Moore is believed to have suffered an AC joint sprain in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions, and while the injury isn’t considered serious, sources familiar with the situation haven’t ruled out the possibility that he’ll miss at least one game. Moore was held without a catch on Thursday after catching five passes for 100 yards and a touchdown in Week 1. Moore’s absence could open the door for Keon Coleman to see more work. Coleman played on 55 snaps against the Lions after playing on just 29 in Week 1, and caught all six of his targets for 63 yards.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Dawson Knox caught both targets for five yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions.
item.description:
Dawson Knox BUF Tight End

Knox cashed in on a touchdown grab from one yard out in the second quarter for his first score of the season. While his snaps should remain high in an offense that rotates pass-catchers at an elevated rate, his primary contribution remains his blocking prowess. He remains a player unlikely to contribute meaningful counting stats on a weekly basis and is best left on the waiver wire.

item.title: Khalil Shakir caught 3-of-6 targets for 38 yards in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions.
item.description:
Khalil Shakir BUF Wide Receiver

Shakir continued in a gadgety role for the Bills, primarily working the short areas of the field in addition to receiving snaps out of the backfield. That could change in the immediate future after lead receiver DJ Moore departed in the second quarter with what appeared to be a significant shoulder injury. Even so, Shakir is best left on the waiver wire in all but the deepest fantasy leagues.

item.title: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) practiced in full on Thursday,
item.description:
Cooper Kupp SEA Wide Receiver

The 33-year-old wide receiver should play in Week 2 against the Cardinals, although he is just a boom-bust FLEX starter at this point. Kupp does not need to be in 12-team lineups.

Source: Josh Weinfuss

item.title: Cardinals TE Trey McBride (rest/back) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Trey McBride ARI Tight End

McBride should be considered good to go for the Cardinals’ Week 2 game against the Seahawks. It took a while for the team to let us know what was going on yesterday. Although there is something at play here with the back listing, the fact that the team labeled it a rest day is great to see. He’s an elite TE1.

Source: Josh Weinfuss

item.title: Lions declared RT Blake Miller, LG Christian Mahogany, CB Keith Abney, EDGE Ahmed Hassanein, CB Ennis Rakestraw, LB Jimmy Rolder and DL Mekhi Wingo inactive for Week 2 against the Bills.
item.description:
Blake Miller DET Tackle

Losing Miller and Mahogany for this one is unfortunate, especially with C Cade Mays (wrist) on injured reserve. The Bills, however, lost DT Ed Oliver to a pre-game hip injury. This should be a high-scoring, fantasy-friendly game environment tonight. Lions CB D.J. Reed (foot) will play.

Source: Chris Brown

item.title: Bills declared RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) inactive for Week 2 against the Lions.
item.description:
Ty Johnson BUF Running Back

Johnson mainly serves as a third-down specialist, so his absence is not hugely consequential. The Bills promoted RB Frank Fore Jr. from the practice squad. He and RB Ray Davis will back up starting RB James Cook tonight.

item.title: The Bills declared DT Ed Oliver, WR Skyler Bell, RB Ty Johnson, S Jalon Kilgore, OG Armaj Reed-Adams, OL Jude Bowry and DL T.J. Sanders inactive for Week 2 against the Lions.
item.description:
Ed Oliver BUF Defensive Lineman

This is a stunner. Oliver’s 2025 season was derailed by injuries, and now the Bills will be without their star interior defender in a tough matchup against the Lions tonight. The Bills entered the game with an advantage in the trenches. The Lions are missing three starting linemen. Oliver’s absence evens the odds a tad.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Bengals QB Joe Burrow (back tightness) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Joe Burrow CIN Quarterback

We knew Burrow was practicing, but we did not know whether he would upgrade to full participation. He remains limited, but beat reporters note that Burrow did far more today than he did yesterday. The Bengals’ quarterback skipped stretches before doing some light throwing on Wednesday. Today, he was suited up in pads and appeared to do everything up through individual drills. He likely sat out team drills, but that is not overly concerning. Burrow should be good to go as a QB1 this week. Hopefully, he upgrades to full participation tomorrow.

Source: Paul Dehner Jr.

item.title: Texans EDGE Jadeveon Clowney (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Jadeveon Clowney HOU Defensive End

Clowney is the type of veteran who can play without practicing, but at this point, he is firmly questionable to play. Fortunately, the Texans field a deep, talented pass rush and will be okay without him.

Source: Houston Texans

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Bills “want to get that running game recharged” in Week 2 against the Lions.
item.description:
James Cook BUF Running Back

Bills RB James Cook totaled 57 yards on just 13 rushing attempts last week, adding three catches for 12 yards. Per Fowler, the Bills plan to use him a lot more in primetime this evening. Cook can be treated as a locked-in RB1 in what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment on Thursday Night Football. The Bills notably elevated RB Frank Gore Jr. from the practice squad, which could indicate that RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) will be inactive tonight.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Free agent WR Brandin Cooks worked out for the Ravens on Thursday.
item.description:
Brandin Cooks

This is probably a bad sign regarding WR Zay Flowers’ (hamstring) Week 2 availability, though the Ravens also placed rookie WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) on short-term injured reserve this week. A signing seems likely.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill reports that Saints WR Chris Olave (hamstring) “left practice as a precautionary measure” on Thursday.
item.description:
Chris Olave NO Wide Receiver

Underhill adds that Olave’s hamstring issue is not expected to be a “problem.” If this really is a non-issue, perhaps Olave just experienced cramping today and will be back out there on Friday, practicing in full. That said, soft tissue issues that pop up mid-week are typically not good. Saints No. 2 WR Devaughn Vele is worth adding if he is a free agent.

Source: Nick Underhill

item.title: Joey Porter Jr. (conditioning, back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

The back designation is new. He left practice with the training staff on Thursday. It seems likely that he reaggravated his existing back injury. Based on that, it wouldn’t be surprising if he remained sidelined for Week 2.

item.title: Saints EDGE Chase Young (calf) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Chase Young NO Defensive End

As it was with Chris Olave, media reporters for the Saints witnessed Young practicing early, so this likely came on afterwards. A midweek downgrade is never a great sign, and Young struggled through a calf injury early last season that sidelined him for some time. Still, it’s not completely implausible he’ll suit up in Week 2. New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill later added that Young experienced “some soreness in his calf,” but “initial opinions are optimistic.”

Source: Nick Underhill

item.title: Chris Olave (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Chris Olave NO Wide Receiver

Olave was added to the injury report after not being on it at all on Wednesday. Saints reporter Mike Triplett said that Olave was spotted during the option portion of media practice. This is fairly concerning, though we have scant information on the injury at this point. Friday’s status will be enormous for Olave.

item.title: Bears RT Darnell Wright (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Darnell Wright CHI Offensive Lineman

Wright’s return and OT Ozzy Trapilo’s continued limited participation are both great signs. The Bears will need Wright against the Vikings’ aggressive, blitz-based defense on Sunday. Trapilo is working his way back from a season-ending patellar tendon rupture and has reportedly been making great progress.

Source: Chicago Bears

item.title: Jets EDGE Will McDonald (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Will McDonald NYJ Defensive End

The midweek downgrade is never a promising sign, and the Jets were definitely hoping to have a full complement of pass-rushers against a beleaguered Packers offensive line in Week 2. Assuming this wasn’t a practice injury that spirals into an extended absence, we’d expect McDonald to be listed as questionable tomorrow.

item.title: Bears RB Kyle Monanga (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

Monangai’s continued participation is a good sign, but soft tissue injuries can be finicky. It would be really nice to see him practice in full tomorrow. If that is indeed the case, Monangai can be started as a high-upside FLEX. Continue monitoring his status. The Bears list RB Roschon Johnson as the next player up.

Source: Chicago Bears

item.title: Bears RB D’Andre Swift (ankle/knee) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
D'Andre Swift CHI Running Back

Swift should be good to go for the Bears’ Week 2 game against the Vikings, though ideally he will upgrade to full participation tomorrow. Swift has achieved borderline RB1/2 status at this point and could make the leap into the top-12. Bears coach Ben Johnson hopes to set the NFL’s scoring record this season and Swift should lead the team in touches each week.

Source: Chicago Bears

item.title: Ladd McConkey (ribs) is working off to the side of the practice with a trainer on Thursday.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

In other words: He’s not actually practicing. It’s generally good news that McConkey has been spotted near the team, but we’re going to need to see a major turnaround on Friday to do better than a questionable tag for the 2024 second-round pick.

Source: Kris Rhim

item.title: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

Okonkwo missed most of the second half of Week 1 and has not been spotted at practice since. There are probably better TE2 bets to lay for Week 2 even if he does suit up in some form on Friday.

item.title: Saints TE Juwan Johnson (illness) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Juwan Johnson NO Tight End

Johnson is firmly on track to play. Illness-related absences are very rare, and the Saints’ No. 1 tight end is already back at it. The Saints face the Ravens this weekend, in what should be a high-scoring game environment. Johnson is a locked-in TE1.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Anthony Richardson (groin) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Anthony Richardson IND Quarterback

Perhaps the groin issue was just maintenance. Either way, Richardson is unlikely to be in line for any work in Week 2. The question here is simply if Richardson will back up Daniel Jones in Week 2 or if Riley Leonard will have to pick up the slack.

item.title: Commanders waived DT Ricky Barber.
item.description:
Ricky Barber

The second-year player is headed to waivers. The Commanders correspondingly promoted CB Isaac Yiadom to the active roster. Barber could be re-signed to the practice squad.

Source: Washington Commanders

item.title: Colts RB DJ Giddens (knee) was added to the injury report and did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
DJ Giddens IND Running Back

He did not play behind Seth McGowan in Week 1 and neither of them have fantasy value while Jonathan Taylor is healthy.

item.title: Alec Pierce (heel) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

It looks like it’s just a routine day off, but we’ll check back on Friday. The Indianapolis Star reported that Pierce told reporters before the practice that the plan is “to put him on the field more in Kansas City” in Week 2 after he played just 59 percent of the team’s snaps.

Source: Indianapolis Star

item.title: Aaron Rodgers said he’s “going to keep feeding” DK Metcalf.
item.description:
DK Metcalf PIT Wide Receiver

Metcalf caught just 4-of-10 targets in Week 1 and was flagged twice for offensive pass interference while struggling to make contested catches. It wasn’t ideal. But Rodgers’ words should sooth any thought of bumping Metcalf down the ranks just yet. “I’m not worried about DK at all, man,” Rodgers said.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) remained limited at Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

We’re not really seeing anything concerning about Coker’s status for Week 2 after he was spotted in a boot following Week 1’s loss to the Bears. He said he’d play and he’s been on the field for two limited sessions in a row. He’ll be in the WR3 tier for Week 2’s matchup against the Falcons assuming nothing calamitous happens on Friday.

item.title: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said the team plans on utilizing TE Oronde Gadsden’s skillset.
item.description:
Oronde Gadsden II LAC Tight End

McDaniel was asked why Gadsden only played eight snaps in Week 1. The Chargers’ offensive coordinator said he expected Gadsden to get more involved last week, but the game “didn’t play out” that way. McDaniel closed by saying he expects Gadsden “to be more involved outside of an unforeseen situation where the game and the parameters with which you’re playing change — and therein lies the problem. Gadsden is not a full-time player. Projecting his weekly usage will be challenging. He is currently not worth starting in 12-team leagues, though that could change if McDaniel decides to feature him.

Source: Kris Rhim

item.title: Brock Bowers (knee) was not participating in the media-viewing portion of practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Every once in a while we’ll get a surprise limited session out of one of these, but it sure looks like Bowers is trending towards questionable-at-best on Friday’s final injury report. The star tight end is trying to come back from a meniscus trim. If he does not play, Michael Mayer will likely pick up the majority of the slack at tight end and be a reasonable streamer TE for Week 2 against the Chargers.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Ravens OC Declan Doyle said he was trying to get WR Rashod Bateman the ball more.
item.description:
Rashod Bateman BAL Wide Receiver

Bateman caught 1-of-2 targets in Week 1, but the catch was erased by a penalty. Bateman, 26, has never established himself as a reliable contributor. Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) is ailing and WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is on injured reserve. Those factors, coupled with Doyle’s comments, could result in one or two plays designed for Bateman early in the Ravens’ Week 2 game against the Saints, but Bateman’s long, unproductive history suggests he is not about to handle a big-time workload. He is not a recommended FLEX starter in 12-team leagues.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Dolphins QB Malik Willis said he knows he must take fewer sacks in Week 2 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Malik Willis MIA Quarterback

Willis stood in the pocket, holding onto the ball too long when trailing the Raiders in the second half last week. He is currently nursing a toe injury, though scrambling faster, or at least throwing on the run, might help him achieve his new goal. Checking down to explosive RB De’Von Achane would also be smart, but the South Florida Sun-Sentinel’s David Furones instead highlighted Willis’ strong connection with rookie WR Caleb Douglas in his article on the subject. Getting the ball out of his hands quickly to either player would be a smart move. Willis’ Dolphins will likely be trailing often in the second half. Developing go-to responses to this situation would help out all involved for fantasy purposes.

Source: South Florida Sun-Sentinel

item.title: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) said he is “ready to go” for Week 2 against the Steelers.
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

This was already apparent, given his full practice participation, but it is nice to hear. The Patriots will have their RB2 on hand for their second game of the season. Starting RB Rhamondre Stevenson will maintain an RB2-worthy workload, but the Patriots need Henderson to deliver chunk gains. Projecting 10 or so touches for Henderson is reasonable. He is a big-play-based FLEX.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Giants RB Tyrone Tracy (illness) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Tyrone Tracy NYG Running Back

Tracy should be good to go for Week 2 sideline duties, though RB Najee Harris could leapfrog him on the depth chart at some point. Tracy does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues after being benched for a fumble in Week 1.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Tua Tagovailoa ATL Quarterback

Tagovailoa seems to be heading toward his second missed game, which probably does not change much for the Falcons’ offense. Falcons QB Michael Penix (knee) is still not ready to play, per a report from earlier this week, though he is splitting first-team reps with QB Cooper Rush (back).

Source: D. Orlando Ledbetter

item.title: Bengals QB Joe Burrow (back tightness) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Joe Burrow CIN Quarterback

At this very moment, Burrow is suited up for practice, participating in warm-ups as he normally would. The official injury report will reveal whether he was limited or a full participant, but what we’ve seen thus far is a great sign. Consider Burrow a fantasy football QB1 unless we get news indicating otherwise.

Source: Paul Dehner Jr.

item.title: Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy said the team is going to continue building up WR Cyrus Allen to a bigger workload “the right way.”
item.description:
Cyrus Allen KC Wide Receiver

Apparently, that means barely using him on game day, at least in the short term. Allen played one snap in the Chiefs’ season opener, despite starting WRs Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy combining for a just 5/37/1 stat line. Bieniemy also said that Allen is “going to be a part of our success moving forward. I guarantee that.” Given Allen’s Week 1 usage, becoming fantasy-relevant could take quite some time.

Source: Charles Goldman

item.title: Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

This could just be a rest day, though those typically happen on Wednesday. Pierce has been working his way back from his offseason heel/ankle surgery, and he reportedly had his wrist X-rayed after the Colts’ Week 1 game against the Ravens. Hopefully, the beat reporters turn up something useful.

Source: Joel A. Erickson

item.title: Ravens LT Ronnie Stanley (toe) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Ronnie Stanley BAL Tackle

Stanley and LG John Simpson (groin) are both missing their second Week 2 practice. Entrenched veterans can sometimes play without practice, but this situation is worth monitoring. Playing without the left side of the offensive line would be suboptimal for the offense.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Early reports regarding Flowers’ health and Week 2 availability were positive, but two missed practices put him firmly in the questionable camp, with a lean toward sitting. Flowers and TE Mark Andrews banked six targets apiece last week and were the only Ravens who cleared three. With WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) on injured reserve, Andrews should handle another sizable workload. Ravens WRs Elijah Sarratt and Devontez Walker should both be active if Flowers sits.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: Steelers WR Michael Pittman (foot) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

Pittman was limited yesterday, before no-showing during the portion of practice open to the media today. Typically, that series of events suggests the player suffered an injury during practice. He should be considered questionable to play in Week 2 against the Patriots at this point. Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth could end up being the biggest beneficiary, potentially operating as the team’s No. 2 target earner if Pittman cannot play.

Source: Nick Farabaugh

item.title: Joey Porter Jr. left practice early with a trainer on Thursday.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

Porter Jr. missed all of training camp with a back injury and then sat out of Week 1 after getting in three limited practices. The team removed his back injury from their report this week, only listing him as limited for conditioning reasons and rest on Wednesday. Mike McCarthy told reporters the plan was for him to do more today. That clearly isn’t happening. It’s unclear if the back issue flared up again or if this is something new. Either way, Porter Jr. appears to be on the wrong side of questionable for Week 2.

Source: Brooke Pryor

item.title: Nico Collins (hamstring) was not seen at Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Nico Collins HOU Wide Receiver

Collins suffered a hamstring injury during Wednesday’s practice and his status for Week 2 is now up in the air. NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports it is a grade one hamstring strain. A DNP today is a bad sign for his availability, though the Texans may take things down to the wire given his importance to the team. Fantasy managers should make contingency plans in case Collins is ruled out before Sunday’s game against the Bengals. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte will have some low-end FLEX appeal versus the Bengals if Collins doesn’t suit up.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Browns signed Jimmy Horn Jr., formerly of the Panthers.
item.description:
Jimmy Horn CLE Wide Receiver

Carolina waived Horn Jr. earlier this week after he muffed a punt in Week 1. NFL insider Jordan Schultz was first on this news, though he didn’t note whether Horn Jr. will be joining the Browns’ active roster or practice squad. We suspect the latter.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Nico Collins’ status for Week 2 against the Bengals “is in jeopardy” because of his hamstring injury.
item.description:
Nico Collins HOU Wide Receiver
